item.title: Pacers host Mavs with Tyrese Haliburton back on home court
item.description: Indianapolis will welcome back Tyrese Haliburton, who helped transform the Indiana Pacers into contenders, while Cooper Flagg will look to continue his emergence for the visiting Dallas Mavericks when the teams square off Friday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Indianapolis will welcome back Tyrese Haliburton, who helped transform the Indiana Pacers into contenders, while Cooper Flagg will look to continue his emergence for the visiting Dallas Mavericks when the teams square off Friday. It will be the first home game in 490 days for Haliburton, who missed all of last season after tearing his right Achilles in Game 7 of the 2025 NBA Finals. In the Pacers' season opener, Haliburton flashed the form that made him a two-time All-Star, scoring 23 points and handing out 12 assists in a 123-120 road victory over the New Orleans Pelicans. After the game, Haliburton acknowledged the emotions surrounding his comeback. "I didn't think I was going to cry," he said. "But there was a moment where it just all hit me." Haliburton's return gives Indiana renewed optimism after the Pacers went 19-63 in his absence last season. Reunited with Pascal Siakam, Haliburton hopes to help Indiana recapture the form that carried them to The Finals two seasons ago. Siakam finished with a game-high 30 points against the Pelicans. "You can't take Pascal Siakam for granted," Indiana coach Rick Carlisle said. "... He's so consistent and makes it look so consistently easy." Carlisle said Quenton Jackson was the "hero of the game" against New Orleans after posting six points, four rebounds and three steals in 16 minutes off the bench. "He earned his way into crunch time," Carlisle said. "That's what we need. We need guys playing their hearts out. Anything less isn't going to get us there." The Mavericks fell 128-110 on the road to the Houston Rockets in their season opener, spoiling Dusty May's debut as Dallas coach. Flagg, however, continued his ascent as a dynamic scorer, pouring in a game-high 32 points. It was the highest-scoring performance by a teenager in an NBA season opener, adding another milestone for the 2025 No. 1 overall pick and reigning NBA Rookie of the Year. Flagg also made 11 of 13 free throw attempts. "That's been a point of emphasis," May said. "When we evaluated ourselves after four (preseason) games, getting to the line wasn't something we did well. We thought (Flagg) was the best way to capitalize on that in the paint." Dallas also welcomed back an All-Star guard from a lengthy injury absence. Kyrie Irving scored 15 points in his first game since tearing his left ACL on March 3, 2025. The Mavericks are still working to unlock their offense with Irving back in the lineup alongside Flagg. "(Irving) is obviously a focal point," May said. "There are going to be puzzles we have to figure out. ... We've got to do a better job and find solutions there." The Mavericks trailed Houston 70-38 at halftime after being outscored 38-12 in the second quarter. Flagg pointed to the team's recurring struggles in those 12 minutes. "The thing for us, all preseason has been second quarters," Flagg said. "We've had bad second quarters going into the half. We have to come out and dig ourselves out of a hole in the third quarter. We have to find a way to combat that and have better second quarters." --Field Level Media

item.title: Putin diz que negociações precisam se concentrar na segurança da Rússia, da Ucrânia e da Europa como um todo
item.description: O presidente russo, Vladimir Putin, afirmou nesta quinta-feira que as futuras negociações para a resolução da guerra na Ucrânia deveriam se concentrar em garantias de segurança para ambos os países e em um quadro geral de segurança em toda a Europa.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O presidente russo, Vladimir Putin, afirmou nesta quinta-feira que as futuras negociações para a resolução da guerra na Ucrânia deveriam se concentrar em garantias de segurança para ambos os países e em um quadro geral de segurança em toda a Europa. Putin, entrevistado pela televisão russa um dia após se reunir com o enviado presidencial dos EUA, Steve Witkoff, confirmou que a Rússia está pronta para retomar as negociações com a Ucrânia, mediadas pelos EUA, no próximo mês. Ele reafirmou a política de longa data do Kremlin de que a Rússia nunca quis iniciar uma guerra, mas enfrentou reações hostis da Ucrânia em questões-chave que preocupam Moscou. As negociações sobre diversos assuntos poderiam levar a um resultado positivo, disse ele, mas a Rússia continuava empenhada em uma solução que pusesse fim ao conflito, em vez de um cessar-fogo de curta duração. “O objetivo dessas negociações será garantir a segurança da Ucrânia e da Rússia após a conclusão de acordos de paz, em sua forma definitiva, e não como resultado de um cessar-fogo temporário por um curto período de tempo. Estamos prontos para retomar esses contatos a fim de alcançar esse objetivo”, disse Putin. O presidente russo disse que Witkoff também enfatizou que as discussões deveriam se estender à “arquitetura da segurança europeia como um todo. E eu concordo com isso também. Bem, vamos ver como as coisas se desenvolvem nos próximos dias.” O presidente ucraniano, Volodymyr Zelenskiy, que se reuniu com Witkoff na Noruega na terça-feira, disse que a Ucrânia está pronta para negociações que provavelmente ocorrerão no início do próximo mês. A Ucrânia, afirmou ele, apoia “quaisquer propostas de cessar-fogo, fim da guerra, cessar-fogo energético, bem como iniciativas humanitárias”. Os esforços liderados pelos Estados Unidos para promover as negociações estagnaram em fevereiro com o início do conflito dos EUA e Israel com o Irã. Muitas das questões relacionadas à guerra na Ucrânia se concentram no território, com a Rússia exigindo que a Ucrânia ceda toda a região de Donbas, no leste do país. Kiev rejeita qualquer ideia de abrir mão dos territórios que atualmente controla. Em seus comentários, Putin disse que qualquer discussão sobre territórios no leste da Ucrânia teria de levar em consideração o que, segundo ele, é o fato de que a região é “historicamente terra russa”. E os moradores da região, disse ele, votaram a favor de fazer parte da Rússia em referendos realizados sete meses após Moscou ter iniciado sua invasão. “Em primeiro lugar, minha posição sobre esse assunto é que esse não é o território deles. É o território da Rússia histórica”, afirmou ele.

item.title: Trump y World Liberty son demandados por operaciones cripto vinculadas a Emiratos Árabes Unidos
item.description: J. Benjamin Greenberg, accionista de Circle, alega que dos transacciones de World Liberty con Emiratos Árabes Unidos violaron la Cláusula de Emolumentos Extranjeros y perjudicaron económicamente a los ...
item.dc:creator: Bob Van Voris, Olga Kharif
item.content:encoded: Bloomberg — Donald Trump y World Liberty Financial, la empresa de criptomonedas que cofundó junto con sus hijos, han sido demandados por un accionista de una empresa rival del sector de las criptomonedas, quien alega que el presidente se benefició ilegalmente de su cargo, infringiendo así la Constitución de los Estados Unidos. J. Benjamin Greenberg, accionista de Circle Internet Group Inc. ( CRCL ), alega que la competencia desleal por parte de World Liberty le ha perjudicado económicamente a él y a otros inversores de Circle. La demanda alega que Trump infringió la Cláusula de Emolumentos Extranjeros, una disposición de la Constitución de los Estados Unidos que prohíbe a los presidentes aceptar pagos de gobiernos extranjeros sin la aprobación del Congreso, en dos transacciones de World Liberty con los Emiratos Árabes Unidos. Ver más: World Liberty de Trump: los planes cripto que anunció y que aún no se han concretado “Esta demanda se refiere a que el presidente de los Estados Unidos se ha beneficiado de forma corrupta de más de US$2.000 millones en pagos de un gobierno extranjero, lo que supone una violación directa de la Constitución”, afirmó Greenberg en una demanda presentada el jueves ante un tribunal federal de Washington. “Ningún presidente en la historia de Estados Unidos se ha beneficiado de su cargo de forma tan descarada”. Trump declaró el año pasado unos ingresos de US$1.400 millones relacionados con sus empresas de criptomonedas, incluida World Liberty. La revelación provocó una fuerte reacción por parte de los demócratas en el Congreso y se le ha atribuido, en parte, el fracaso de la Ley de Claridad (Clarity Act), que se suponía que iba a establecer normas de estructura de mercado para el sector de las criptomonedas. Según Greenberg, la venta de una participación del 49% en World Liberty por US$500 millones a un vehículo de inversión respaldado por un miembro de la familia gobernante de los Emiratos Árabes Unidos y la compra, por parte del fondo MGX de Abu Dabi, de la stablecoin de World Liberty para financiar una transacción de US$2.000 millones constituían una infracción de la legislación estadounidense. Ver más: Este fondo cripto se resiste a la fiebre de la IA y mantiene su apuesta por los activos digitales Greenberg presentó su denominada demanda derivada en calidad de accionista individual de Circle con el fin de reclamar una indemnización por daños y perjuicios en nombre de la empresa. Afirma que los accionistas sufrieron perjuicios económicos a causa de World Liberty, que compite con Circle en el mercado de las stablecoins . “Esta demanda ha sido presentada por un accionista particular, no por Circle”, declaró un portavoz de la empresa en respuesta a la demanda. “Circle no inició, dirigió, autorizó ni participó en la presentación de la misma”. Un portavoz de World Liberty afirmó que las alegaciones “carecen de fundamento”. “World Liberty Financial cumple con todas las leyes y normativas estadounidenses”, declaró David Wachsman en un comunicado. “Nadie en World Liberty Financial trabaja para el Gobierno de los Estados Unidos”. Ver más: Bitcoin cae por debajo de US$82.000 ante temores por la IA que afectan al mercado El Departamento de Justicia no respondió de inmediato a una solicitud de comentarios. La administración Trump ha negado que las iniciativas del presidente en el ámbito de las criptomonedas planteen conflictos. Este caso se suma a varias acciones judiciales interpuestas contra Trump durante su primer mandato presidencial, que finalizó en 2021, en las que se alegaban violaciones de la Cláusula de Emolumentos y se le criticaba por haberse beneficiado indebidamente de la presidencia. Ninguna de las demandas logró recuperar dinero del presidente ni obligarle a poner fin a las prácticas empresariales que, según alegaban, eran inconstitucionales. Trump y sus hijos cofundaron World Liberty meses antes de las elecciones de 2024. La empresa emitió dos tokens: el WLFI y la stablecoin USD1. El fondo MGX de Abu Dabi utilizó esta stablecoin el año pasado para adquirir una participación de US$2.000 millones en Binance, la mayor plataforma de intercambio de criptomonedas del mundo. Ver más: JPMorgan ve al bitcoin superando a las acciones, pero advierte sobre un riesgo La stablecoin tiene actualmente una capitalización de mercado de unos US$4.000 millones, según el rastreador CoinGecko. World Liberty ya se encuentra inmersa en una batalla legal con el multimillonario Justin Sun, quien acusó a la empresa de congelar ilegalmente sus tokens WLFI y de extorsión. World Liberty, a su vez, le demandó por difamación. La demanda contra Trump y World Liberty solicita una orden que impida al presidente infringir la Cláusula de Emolumentos Extranjeros, así como la devolución de las ganancias ilegales y una indemnización por daños y perjuicios sin especificar. El caso es Greenberg contra Trump, 26-cv-03686, Tribunal de Distrito de los Estados Unidos, Distrito de Columbia (Washington). Lea más en Bloomberg.com

item.title: Hadjar riles Leclerc by saying Verstappen would be faster in a Ferrari
item.description: Isack Hadjar riled rival Charles Leclerc by suggesting Ferrari had the fastest car and Red Bull teammate Max Verstappen would have won this month's Singapore Grand Prix by an even greater margin if he had been driving for the Italian team.
item.dc:creator: Alan Baldwin
item.content:encoded: Isack Hadjar riled rival Charles Leclerc by suggesting Ferrari had the fastest car and Red Bull teammate Max Verstappen would have won this month's [USN:L1N45X03I TEXT:"Singapore Grand Prix"] by an even greater margin if he had been driving for the Italian team. Leclerc, who finished second in the race and 7.3 seconds behind four-time Formula One champion Verstappen, dismissed the Frenchman's claims at the US Grand Prix on Thursday. "I think it's nonsense to start saying these kinds of things. Isack has no idea what kind of car we drive, and I have no idea what kind of car he drives," the Monegasque told reporters at Austin's Circuit of the Americas. Hadjar, who finished 10th in Singapore, said the Red Bull car was still very hard to drive even if Verstappen has now won the last two races. "In Malaysia, it (the Red Bull) was dominant, but I don't think in Singapore it was the fastest car. That's what I believe. I think if you put Max in the Ferrari, he would have won the race with more margin. So that's my opinion. In Singapore, I think it (the Ferrari) was the fastest car," he said. McLaren's Oscar Piastri said both rivals were stronger than the reigning champions. "I think it wasn't a surprise that Ferrari were very strong in Singapore. I think on the data analysis, they're always the quickest or joint-quickest or outright quickest in basically every corner this year," the Australian said. "But they lose on all the straights, whether that's from drag or power, I don't know ... but we've expected them (Ferrari) to be the benchmark at other circuits and it's not turned out to be the case. I think they're very strong. I think clearly Red Bull was very strong. Both stronger than us for sure. "I think over the last few weeks Red Bull has definitely become the most consistently quick car. But I think each weekend the challenges are kind of rotating."

item.title: Japan's core inflation exceeds BOJ target, cements near-term rate hike chance
item.description: Japan's core consumer inflation exceeded the central bank's 2% target in September for the first time in nine months, data showed on Friday, a sign of broadening price pressure that cements the case for a near-term interest rate hike.
item.dc:creator: Leika Kihara, Takahiko Wada
item.content:encoded: Japan's core consumer inflation exceeded the central bank's 2% target in September for the first time in nine months, data showed on Friday, a sign of broadening price pressure that cements the case for a near-term interest rate hike. The figures underscored how higher fuel costs from the prolonged Middle East conflict, elevated import prices driven by the weak yen and price pressures from robust AI demand were blunting the impact of government fuel subsidies. Having just raised interest rates last month, the Bank of Japan is set to stand pat on policy next week but may revise up its inflation forecast and signal its readiness to keep pushing up still-low borrowing costs, [USN:L4N4650KC TEXT:"sources have told Reuters"]. "Core inflation is expected to accelerate due to rising energy costs from the Middle East conflict and subsequent second-round effects," said Masato Koike, a senior economist at Sompo Institute Plus. "But with price rises not accelerating sharply, there's little need for a back-to-back rate increase in October," he said, projecting the BOJ's next hike to come in December. The core consumer price index (CPI), which excludes volatile fresh food but includes fuel costs, rose 2.1% in September from a year earlier, data showed, matching a median market forecast and accelerating from a 1.7% rise in August. An index that strips away the effects of both volatile fresh food and fuel, which is closely watched by the BOJ as a better gauge of demand-driven price pressures, rose 2.4% in September from a year earlier after increasing 1.9% in August. In a sign of broadening inflationary pressure, goods prices rose 2.8% year-on-year in September, accelerating from a 2.6% gain in August, the data showed. Services inflation also accelerated to 1.5% in September from 1.2% in the previous month, suggesting firms were passing on higher labour costs from a tight job market. RISK OF HIGHER TERMINAL RATE The data will be among factors the BOJ will scrutinise in producing fresh quarterly growth and price forecasts at next week's two-day policy meeting ending on October 30. [USN:L4N45S011 TEXT:"Sources have told Reuters"] the BOJ may signal that underlying inflation - or the broad price trend stripping away temporary, one-off factors - likely achieved 2%, and stress its focus on anchoring inflation around the target. Governor Kazuo Ueda said [USN:L1N4620G5 TEXT:"last week"] the BOJ won't tolerate any inflation overshoot, signalling resolve to continue raising rates after lifting them to a 31-year high of 1.25% [USN:L1N459138 TEXT:"last month"]. [USN:L1N468046 TEXT:"Recent surveys"] showed few signs past rate hikes were cooling loan demand, suggesting scope for further rate increases and drawing attention to the BOJ's assessment on lending conditions. Many analysts [USN:L4N4650G0 TEXT:"polled by Reuters"] expect the BOJ to raise its policy rate to 1.50% in December, and predict the terminal rate to be around 1.75% or 2%. Marcel Thieliant, head of Asia-Pacific at Capital Economics, projects the BOJ to leave policy steady next week but signal continued concerns about upside risks to inflation. "With little evidence that the tightening delivered so far has slowed the economy, the risks are shifting towards a higher peak in the policy rate than our forecast of 2%," Thieliant said.

TOKYO, Oct 23 : Japan's annual core consumer inflation exceeded the central bank's 2 per cent target in September for the first time in nine months, data showed on Friday, a sign of broadening price pressure that cements the case for a near-term interest rate hike. The figures underscored how higher fuel costs from the prolonged Middle East conflict, elevated import prices driven by the weak yen and price pressures from robust AI demand were blunting the impact of government fuel subsidies. Having just raised interest rates last month, the Bank of Japan is set to stand pat on policy next week but may revise up its inflation forecast and signal its readiness to keep pushing up still-low borrowing costs, sources have told Reuters. The core consumer price index (CPI), which excludes volatile fresh food but includes fuel costs, rose 2.1 per cent in September from a year earlier, data showed, matching a median market forecast. It followed a 1.7 per cent rise in August.

An index that strips away the effects of both volatile fresh food and fuel, which is closely watched by the BOJ as a better gauge of demand-driven price pressures, rose 2.4 per cent in September from a year earlier after increasing 1.9 per cent in August. The BOJ raised its key rate to a 31-year high of 1.25 per cent last month, signalling a shift to guarding against underlying inflation overshooting its target and raising the prospect of additional rate hikes. BOJ Governor Kazuo Ueda has warned that underlying inflation, or the broad price trend stripping away temporary, one-off factors, may overshoot its 2 per cent target on price pressures from the Middle East conflict, a weak yen and brisk AI demand.

item.title: 米俳優トム・スケリットさん死去、93歳 「トップガン」など出演
item.description:
Will Dunham
[２２日 ロイター] - 映画「エイリアン」や「トップガン」などのヒット作に出演した米俳優トム・スケリットさんが死去した。９３歳だった。遺族の声明によると、２１日に亡くなり、自然死だったという。
精悍な容姿と幅広い役柄をこなす演技で知られ、１９６０年代から２０２０年代にかけて映画やテレビで活躍した。
出世作は、朝鮮戦争を舞台にした７０年のブラックコメディー「Ｍ★Ａ★Ｓ★Ｈ
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Will Dunham

[２２日 ロイター] - 映画「エイリアン」や「トップガン」などのヒット作に出演した米俳優トム・スケリットさんが死去した。９３歳だった。遺族の声明によると、２１日に亡くなり、自然死だったという。

精悍な容姿と幅広い役柄をこなす演技で知られ、１９６０年代から２０２０年代にかけて映画やテレビで活躍した。

出世作は、朝鮮戦争を舞台にした７０年のブラックコメディー「Ｍ★Ａ★Ｓ★Ｈ 　マッシュ」の軍医役。７９年のＳＦホラー「エイリアン」では宇宙船の船長、８６年の「トップガン」では海軍の飛行教官を演じた。

他にも「マグノリアの花たち」「リバー・ランズ・スルー・イット」「コンタクト」などに出演。テレビドラマ「ピケット・フェンス　ブロック捜査メモ」では、９３年にエミー賞のドラマ部門主演男優賞を受賞した。

ミシガン州デトロイト生まれ。米空軍勤務を経て、６２年に映画デビューした。３度結婚し、５人の子どもをもうけた。

遺族は「ユーモアや好奇心、知恵、寛大さにあふれ、私たちの人生に愛をもたらしてくれた人だった」と追悼した。

item.title: テスラとの統合はマスク氏の承認必要、スペースＸが表明
item.description: [２２日 ロイター] - 米宇宙開発企業スペースＸは２２日、米電気自動車大手テスラ との統合に踏み切る場合は、支配株主...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
テスラとの統合はマスク氏の承認必要、スペースＸが表明 8:39 配信

2025年10月、米テキサス州スターベースで、試験飛行を控えたスペースXの宇宙船「スターシップ」を先導するテスラのサイバートラック。REUTERS/Steve Nesius

[２２日 ロイター] - 米宇宙開発企業スペースＸは２２日、米電気自動車大手テスラ との統合に踏み切る場合は、支配株主であるイーロン・マスク氏の承認が必要になるとの見解を示した。マスク氏は利益相反を理由に両社間の協議からは身を引いている。ただ統合にマスク氏の承認が必要とされたことで、協議に直接関与する関係者は「手続きが複雑化する」と述べ、テスラ株主の利益が十分に代表されているかを巡る疑問が生じかねないとの見方を示した。

マスク氏は２０日、スペースＸとテスラの統合は「良い考えだ」と語り、両社が統合の可能性を検討するため特別委員会を設置したと明らかにしていた。

こうした中でスペースＸは２２日に提出した規制当局向け文書で「特別委員会は統合の可能性に関して何ら決定しておらず、統合案はいかなる場合も特別委員会、取締役会および支配株主による追加承認が必要となる」と説明した。

複数のウォール街アナリストは、テスラとスペースＸの統合は「実現するかどうかではなく、いつ実現するかの問題」とみている一方、統合時にテスラ株主が受け取る対価については見解が分かれている。

またマスク氏が今週、統合計画を公然と支持したことで、協議に関与する関係者の一部に懸念が広がった。関係者によると、同氏の発言で統合協議を巡る公正性の面で、株主の目が厳しくなり、協議の進展を数週間遅らせる可能性があるという。

マスク氏はテスラ株のおよそ５分の１を保有し、スペースＸでは議決権支配権を握る。統合が実現した場合、同氏が統合後の新会社への影響力を一段と強めるとみられる。

ロイター 関連ニュース 焦点：ＮＡＳＡローマン宇宙望遠鏡打ち上げへ、ダークエネルギーやダークマターの解明期待 アングル：米金融大手、第2四半期は軒並み好決算　投資銀・取引部門がけん引 アングル：スペースＸ株が公開価格割れ、投資家の信頼守れるか　他案件に影響も アングル：米国で新たに44万人の「ＡＩ長者」、高級品の支出と嗜好にも変化 焦点：ラッセル指数銘柄入れ替えで26日は米株取引急増か、スペースＸなど注目 最終更新: 10/23(金) 8:39 ロイター

item.title: Hamilton says he could keep going now that African race is planned
item.description: Seven-time world champion Lewis Hamilton said a race in Africa was a dream that could keep him going longer in the sport now that Formula One has done a deal with Rwanda for a grand prix in the early 2030s.
item.dc:creator: Alan Baldwin
item.content:encoded: Seven-time world champion Lewis Hamilton said a race in Africa was a dream that could keep him going longer in the sport now that Formula One has [USN:L6N45Z0M6 TEXT:"done a deal with Rwanda"] for a grand prix in the early 2030s. The Ferrari driver will be 42 in January and has a contract for 2027. Fernando Alonso, the oldest active F1 driver, is 45 and recently [USN:L6N45L0PA TEXT:"signed up for another season"] with Aston Martin. "I'm now forced to stay a lot longer because we have a race in Africa, and that's been my dream, to be able to race in Africa," Hamilton said at the US Grand Prix on Thursday in a press conference alongside championship leader Kimi Antonelli. "I have to keep fighting to try and stay fit. If I can still punch out good results over the next year, we'll keep it going." Antonelli, who replaced Hamilton at Mercedes last season and is still only 20 years old, encouraged him: "You got to do at least the first one." Hamilton, the sport's first and only Black champion, has long campaigned for a race in Africa -- a continent that last hosted a race at South Africa's Kyalami circuit in 1993 -- and spoke of his efforts. "Countless meetings with the stakeholders, so many meetings with (F1 CEO) Stefano (Domenicali) at his office in London, but also on race weekends, countless calls: 'What's happening? Where are we going? Who are you meeting with?' "Many meetings with different presidents from different countries. Lots of phone calls with different presidents from different countries within Africa," he recalled. "I think for me, it's a place that deserves to have a grand prix. It's about more than just one country. It's about the continent itself." Hamilton said an African race would make people more aware of the continent, but recognized there were concerns. Human rights campaigners Amnesty International [USN:L6N45Z0SJ TEXT:"recently accused Formula One"] of hollow words and offering Rwanda a "sportswashing prize" -- an accusation leveled at countries perceived to be using sport to improve a tarnished image abroad. "Of course, I don't get to choose where we go. Naturally, there are problems all over the world today, so I've seen many of the stories. But I think we really have to approach it with humility," Hamilton said. "Of course, going there doesn't mean that you neglect the things that are happening there. So hopefully many people start to educate themselves a little bit more about what is happening there and what has happened there for hundreds of years. I hope that does spark the conversation."

item.title: From Canada to Nigeria, a race for more 'defence sovereignty' is on
item.description: By the time Eliot Pence stood down as head of international operations for US autonomous weapons powerhouse Anduril in 2022, the Canadian-born executive had spent most of his working life in a US-dominated defence-tech sector he says he and his countrymen rarely questioned.
item.dc:creator: Peter Apps
item.content:encoded: By the time Eliot Pence stood down as head of international operations for US autonomous weapons powerhouse Anduril in 2022, the Canadian-born executive had spent most of his working life in a US-dominated defence-tech sector he says he and his countrymen rarely questioned. In the aftermath of the COVID-19 pandemic and with geopolitical tensions rising, increasing volumes of investment were flowing to a new generation of weapons such as those that company built. Insofar as most US allies thought about defence technology, the priority was its ability to interface directly with a fast-evolving US military. Fast forward four years, and that priority remains. But nations are pushing harder and faster than at any point in recent history to regain more sovereignty in their systems. What that shift means varies widely from country to country, but it is developing some increasingly universal themes, including reducing dependence on the United States and a search for supply chains less controlled by China. Pence - who last year founded Dominion Dynamics, a Canadian defence technology company working to establish sovereign capability in aerospace, autonomy and command-and-control - is on the advisory committee on Canada-US economic relations . Canada's previous strategy of sourcing more than 70% of its defence technology requirements from United States, now faced the new reality of a US administration that was "sometimes antagonistic, to put it mildly", he said. "Canada is now effectively needing to rebuild its defence industry from scratch," he told this columnist on the sidelines of this month's London Resilience Conference showcasing new defence technology alongside venture capital. VARYING THREATS, VARYING RESPONSES Many US allies have been alarmed by limitations placed on the SpaceX-run Starshield system relied on by Ukraine for drone operations and President Donald Trump's plan to buy Russian diesel and decision to [USN:L1N46808R TEXT:"waive new Russia sanctions"]. Trump says he is acting in the interests of the United States. Meanwhile Norwegian media reported this month that Chinese-built electric vehicles taking part in Norwegian military drills were found to have silently filmed participants, although it was not clear if that was deliberately triggered. Multiple nations are racing to source non-China supplies of batteries, components and essential minerals and chemicals, with Beijing tightening controls of multiple rare earths last year in its trade dispute with Washington. Beijing has choked off [USN:L4N4660FG TEXT:"Japan's supplies of yttrium"]– used in jet engines, semiconductors and defence systems - since a diplomatic row between them last year. While some nations are keeping quiet about any policy and industrial shifts to avoid antagonising Washington or Beijing, others are speaking out. Canada's Prime Minister Mark Carney has been one of the loudest critics of Trump, calling for "middle powers" to do much more to chart their own global course. Dominion Dynamics said it had raised C$169 million ($118 million), mainly from Canadian investors, by June. Its early products include the Echo sonar surveillance system that it says will help Canada and close allies – particularly other Arctic nations – keep track of their increasingly contested waters. Like others in Canada, Pence was keen to stress that this did not mean an end to Canada’s long-running direct collaboration with the US Northern Command. But it meant those in charge in Ottawa would also have sovereign systems on which they could rely. Last month, Carney told the New York Times military planners had now drawn up at least limited plans for what he called the "extreme tail risk" – a financial phrase referring to an unlikely but plausible scenario – for the defence of Canada from hypothetical future American attack. Since returning to office at the start of 2025, Trump has on several occasions questioned Canada's right to exist and suggested it might become the 51st US state, although he has generally ruled out using military force. Even more overt threats against Denmark suggesting Washington [USN:L6N460097 TEXT:"might seize Greenland"], though, have also unnerved US allies. What nations like the Baltics, Nordics and Poland now fear is that as in Ukraine, future US administrations might cut access to US systems and weapons stocks to push governments towards US-brokered deals costing territory or independence. MILITARY INDUSTRY AND POWER ARE SHIFTING FAST Established military players such as France, Britain, Germany and South Korea have tended to prioritise "big ticket" items such as ships, tanks and submarines that bring significant numbers of jobs in often politically contested regions. Increasingly, however, officials and a new generation of defence firms are looking to what has happened in Ukraine and well beyond and have concluded that the focus needs to shift to cheap, mass producible systems for attack and surveillance. The result, some defence insiders say, may be a swift and dramatic shift in the global shape of both military industry and power, including in unexpected places. One of the key sponsors of the Resilience Conference was Nigeria's Terra Industries, now with some 200 staff working in Abuja to deliver a range of drones including the Archer with a 1,000-km (620-mile) range and the Kallon solar-powered sentry tower providing 24-hour AI surveillance. Founder Nathan Nwachuku quit university in the US to found an educational technology startup first, but changed tack after considering the threat to the international order posed by Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. SOVEREIGN COMMAND-AND-CONTROL FACES CHALLENGES What African nations like Nigeria faced was not the risk of traditional invasion, he said, but more subtle yet potentially lethal intervention by militant groups, state-armed gangs, financial interests and major powers including Moscow and Beijing. Critical to stopping that, he said, was using cheap technology to secure borders and essential infrastructure. "Our central intelligence platform carries out large-scale command and control, autonomous mission planning and threat intelligence across infrastructure," Nwachuku said, adding that at present no Chinese or US company could offer African firms or governments anything like that. Crucially, while the company is Nigerian, when it works with other nations – so far primarily Ghana – it bases its servers in that country to maintain effective national sovereign control. In the background, the US military and its global command structures are also often quietly supportive of smaller nations building up capability separate to that Washington provides. Sometimes, such joint working can cement broader relations between specific allies. Britain is working with Norway on warships as is Japan with Australia while Canberra is also building the Ghost Shark underwater drone with US-based Anduril and aerial Ghost Bat with Boeing. Analysts and diplomats say the role of the [USN:L6N460097 TEXT:"fledgling UK-Italy-Japan"] Future Global Combat Air Program in Japan's defence relationship with Europe is seen in Tokyo as being as critical as the aeroplane itself, while fighting in Ukraine continues to draw in more and more defence contractors of almost every size and type keen for lessons to take home. But such partnerships are often fraught. Politico this week reported Germany pulling back from its planned Ghost Bat purchase, while a [USN:L8N42G1I7 TEXT:"Franco-German fighter project collapsed in June"]. At another summit in London this month, the senior British officer building an Allied Underwater Battlespace Mission Network – bringing together multiple systems and sensors from the US, Australia and much of Europe – complained nationally driven experimentation and duplication risked wasting resources. Russian and Chinese commentators have this week suggested Washington's latest schism with Ukraine may be permanent and point to future breaks with other allies. Other nations will surely need to learn to do much more on their own – but it will take making those efforts work seamlessly together to keep already watching potential enemies deterred.

item.title: Taiwan shuts down ahead of Typhoon Champi, hundreds of flights cancelled
item.description: Almost all of Taiwan shut down on Friday ahead of the arrival of Typhoon Champi, which is forecast to bring strong winds and torrential rain, though the storm is weakening and is not expected to make direct landfall on the island.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Almost all of Taiwan shut down on Friday ahead of the arrival of Typhoon Champi, which is forecast to bring strong winds and torrential rain, though the storm is weakening and is not expected to make direct landfall on the island. At one point a super typhoon and one of the strongest storms in the Pacific this year, Champi was still packing gusts of around 191 kph (119 mph) near its centre, according to Taiwan's Central Weather Administration (CWA). The storm was about 330 km (205 miles) east of Taiwan's southern tip, the CWA said. The storm's forecast track shows it will pass just off northeastern Taiwan, turn north toward the Chinese coast and eventually move into southern Japan. The administration said its radius was around 320 km (200 miles), large enough to cover most of Taiwan, and weather experts said its impact could last nearly two days. Taiwan's financial markets (.TWII) , will also close for Friday, while only the Taiwan-controlled Kinmen islands, which sit next to the Chinese coast, will open schools and offices as normal. The transport ministry said all 262 domestic flights were cancelled for Friday, along with more than 350 international ones. In the capital Taipei there were squally showers, but public transport including the subway was operating as usual, albeit with reduced service. Taiwan is generally very well prepared for typhoons, which keeps casualties low. Although more common in summer, the storms can strike in autumn too. The typhoon is forecast to first pass over Japan's westernmost inhabited island, Yonaguni, in Okinawa Prefecture.

item.title: LeBron James, 76ers ready for home opener despite 'outside noise'
item.description: PHILADELPHIA -- The Eagles were sent scrambling when blood clots sidelined Jalen Hurts, likely for the year. The Flyers opened their season with nine losses in a row.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: PHILADELPHIA -- The Eagles were sent scrambling when blood clots sidelined Jalen Hurts, likely for the year. The Flyers opened their season with nine losses in a row. Now, with an all-time great on the premises, the stage is set for Philadelphia to be a 76ers city. Three months after LeBron James revealed his fourth team and self-proclaimed "last decision," thousands of fans poured in Thursday to witness James' first home opener with Philadelphia. The crowd bellowed when James was announced in pregame introductions, just before franchise centerpiece Joel Embiid, and he followed his teammates onto the court. Soon after, fans found another level when James performed his ritual "chalk toss" on the scorer's table for the first time in his new home. "Obviously it's always great for the city and the energy," 76ers coach Nick Nurse said pregame. "You can feel it in the streets and stuff and around the building." The Sixers, whose last championship came in 1983, opened the season Tuesday by spoiling the New York Knicks' banner-raising at Madison Square Garden with a 106-100 victory. James compiled 14 points, nine rebounds and seven assists in his team debut. Two days later, James arrived at Xfinity Mobile Arena to face the Cleveland Cavaliers, his hometown team and the franchise he'll be associated with first and foremost. An hour and change before tipoff, James, 41, was on the court warming up wearing a short-sleeved hoodie. Elsewhere, 76ers fans filled the stadium concourse, where jerseys with James' No. 23 and the block-lettered PHILA outnumbered jerseys of Embiid, Jaylen Brown and Tyrese Maxey, the team's other stars. Every seat in the arena bore a free white T-shirt commemorating the Sixers' opening night, with caricatures of Nurse and each player, and James near the center. And legendary Philly boxer Bernard Hopkins was on hand to perform the team's pregame "Ring the Bell" custom, ringing a replica of the Liberty Bell. James, who didn't speak before the game, said at the team's preseason media day that he respected Philadelphia basketball culture, from the famed Palestra gymnasium to his experiences as a visiting player. "It's been like, ‘OK, we respect the way you play the game because we know the game, and we know the history of the game and we've seen so many players play the game. But we hate you. You're not with us, we hate you,'" James explained then. "... And I love that. Actually, I really love it. I really thrive under that circumstance. But yeah, it's always been mutual respect, it's always been mutual respect with myself and the Philly fans." Some additional fuel was added to the fire Thursday when, hours before the game, President Donald Trump wrote on his social media platform that James "disrespect(ed) our country" by appearing to mime a golf swing and a jump shot during the pregame performance of the national anthem Tuesday in New York. "I said right from the beginning that he's no good, a TOTAL DISGRACE," Trump wrote. "LeBron James should apologize to all of those Great American Warriors and Heroes who died for the American Flag, and all that our Country stands for!" Nurse was asked pregame how he felt about that extra layer of outside noise, at the start of the 76ers' most anticipated season in recent memory. "I think that goes right in with other outside noise we've already had, right?" Nurse said. "And I kind of keep saying the same thing. All I really care about is getting them to the practice floor, getting them in the film room, getting them to the game floor, and the focus that they've had and the intent and all the stuff they've had has been excellent." During Thursday's rendition of the anthem by Boyz II Men, James appeared to shift in place to stay loose but did not move more than that. --Adam Zielonka, Field Level Media

item.title: 米Ｐ＆Ｇ、コスト増が通期利益を一段と圧迫へ 需要は底堅く
item.description: ［２２日 ロイター］ - 米日用品大手プロクター・アンド・ギャンブル（Ｐ＆Ｇ）は２２日、原材料・エネルギー・輸送コス...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
米Ｐ＆Ｇ、コスト増が通期利益を一段と圧迫へ　需要は底堅く 8:10 配信

プロクター・アンド・ギャンブル（Ｐ＆Ｇ）のロゴ。2025年11月、上海で撮影。REUTERS/Maxim Shemetov

［２２日　ロイター］ - 米日用品大手プロクター・アンド・ギャンブル（Ｐ＆Ｇ）は２２日、原材料・エネルギー・輸送コストの上昇が通期（２０２７年６月期）の利益をより大きく圧迫するとの見通しを示した。一方、美容・ホームケア製品への底堅い需要が第１・四半期（７─９月）の売上高を押し上げた。

コスト上昇による通期の利益下押し額は約１４億ドルになると見込み、従来予想の１０億ドルから引き上げた。

アンドレ・シュルテン最高財務責任者（ＣＦＯ）は記者向け電話会見で、コモディティー価格高騰による圧力は今後２四半期にわたり強まる見通しだと述べた。

ただ、第１・四半期決算が市場予想を上回ったことを受け、Ｐ＆Ｇ株は約６％上昇した。

第１・四半期の純売上高は４％増の２３２億８０００万ドルとなり、ＬＳＥＧがまとめたアナリスト予想の２２８億ドルを上回った。

美容事業の販売数量は増加した。燃料費や食品価格の上昇で家計が圧迫される中でも、消費者はセルフケアへの支出を続けており、高価格帯のヘアケア製品の需要が業績を支えた。
