FAST

Oct 22 : The cost of insuring Meta Platforms' debt against default touched an all-time high on Thursday, as investors grappled with concerns about its plan to spend more on its AI build-out. Meta raised the lower end of its annual forecast for capital expenditure to between $135 billion and $145 billion this year, up from $130 billion to $145 billion expected previously. As a result, five-year credit default swaps widened 7.6 basis points to a record high of 114.79 bps and were set for its biggest one-day jump since at least 2025, Markit data showed. Its shares were last down 6.1 per cent at $655, hitting their lowest in about six weeks. Meta also introduced new non-voting shares and reported a free cash flow deficit of $2.12 billion in the third quarter, turning cash flow negative for the first time since 2012.

"The market has been questioning whether all the spending on AI is having the type of returns that the market originally expected," said Steve Sosnick, chief market analyst at Interactive Brokers. "In Meta's case, investors are interpreting the new non-voting shares as a backdoor for issuing more stock and diluting holdings eventually so I think that's adding to this aggressive selloff." Investors are growing more cautious about debt-fueled AI spending in the face of rising borrowing costs, with neocloud firm CoreWeave at the center of a storm that has erased more than 34 per cent of its market value this month. CoreWeave shares slumped 8.4 per cent on Thursday, while rival Nebius Group and data center operators IREN and Applied Digital also saw heavy losses. US chip stocks, widely viewed as one of the biggest winners of the AI boom, also sold off heavily with the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index set to erase more than $688 billion in market value on Thursday alone. Five-year credit default swaps of hyperscaler Oracle were also close to a record high, while that of Amazon.com held near its highest level since March 2020, according to S&P Global Market Intelligence data. Oracle and Alphabet shares dropped more than 2 per cent, while Microsoft slipped 1.3 per cent and Amazon fell 3.7 per cent.

item.title: 米新規失業保険申請6000件減の19.4万件、約57年ぶり低水準に迫る
item.description: [ワシントン ２２日 ロイター] - 米労働省が２２日発表した１０月１７日までの週の新規失業保険申請件数（季節調整済み）...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
米新規失業保険申請6000件減の19.4万件、約57年ぶり低水準に迫る 10/22 22:46 配信

米バージニア州アーリントンにある店舗に掲げられた求人看板。2023年4月撮影。REUTERS/Elizabeth Frantz

[ワシントン　２２日　ロイター] - 米労働省が２２日発表した１０月１７日までの週の新規失業保険申請件数（季節調整済み）は前週比６０００件減の１９万４０００件となった。レイオフ（一時解雇）の少なさを背景に、申請件数は１９６９年以来の低水準となった７月中旬の１８万９０００件に迫る水準にある。

ロイターがまとめたエコノミスト予想は２０万件だった。

週ごとの変動をならした４週間移動平均は１０００件減の１９万７７５０件と、１９６９年以来の低水準となった。

エコノミストらは、堅調な内需を背景に企業収益が伸びていることに加え、退職の増加やトランプ政権による移民取り締まりで労働力人口が縮小していることが、労働者を解雇から守っていると指摘している。ただ、中東紛争の長期化に伴う金融環境の引き締めや金利上昇が、来年の労働市場に悪影響を及ぼす恐れがあるとの懸念もある。

ＦＷＤＢＯＮＤＳのチーフエコノミスト、クリストファー・ラプキー氏は「政権の移民政策により労働市場は逼迫し、企業は財（モノ）・サービスの生産に必要な人手を確保できなくなっているため、既存の労働者を手放さない状況になっている」と指摘。「多くの産業において、突如として労働者が代替不可能な存在となっている」と述べた。

今回の申請件数データは、１０月の雇用統計の調査期間と重なっている。

１０月１０日までの１週間の継続受給件数（季節調整済み）は２万５０００件増の１７２万８０００件となった。 ただ、継続受給件数には、大学を最近卒業した人や、職歴が浅い、または全くないために受給資格がない人は含まれていない。

長期失業者の一部が、大半の州で２６週間に制限されている受給資格を使い果たした可能性もあり、これが継続受給件数が低水準で推移する一因となっている可能性がある。９月の失業期間の中央値は１１．５週と、約４年半ぶりの高水準に近いものの、９月の失業率は４．２％にとどまっており、労働市場がインフレの要因とはなっていない。

ハイ・フリークエンシー・エコノミクスのチーフエコノ ミスト、カール・ワインバーグ氏は「米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）は、需要を抑制しスラック（需給の緩み）を拡大して、インフレ目標回帰を確実にするために金融引き締めが必要と判断すれば、来週にも自由に利上げに踏み切ることができる」と指摘。「雇用に関するＦＲＢの責務は明らかに満たされている」と述べた。

ロイター 関連ニュース 焦点：ＡＩ信奉の誤算、米メタ　大規模リストラ縮小し「人間中心」に回帰 アングル：米雇用統計、利下げ観測復活の試金石に　ＦＲＢはなお慎重 アングル：3月米雇用統計、ＦＲＢの金利据え置きシナリオの補強要因に 焦点：ＡＩが10万人以上の雇用に影響か、米映画業界でリスキリング活況 アングル：試される米消費の持続力、物価高に政府閉鎖や雇用情勢悪化で 最終更新: 10/23(金) 0:09 ロイター

item.title: Will US Treasury scrap 20-year bond sales?: McGeever
item.description: The US Treasury's auction of 20-year bonds on Wednesday won’t be the last, but this long-term debt instrument's days may be numbered.
item.dc:creator: Jamie McGeever
item.content:encoded: The US Treasury's auction of 20-year bonds on Wednesday won’t be the last, but this long-term debt instrument's days may be numbered. Long-term borrowing costs are high. Yields on 10-year and 30-year Treasuries earlier this month rose to their highest levels since 2002, reaching 5.36% and 5.66%, respectively. The 5.469% that Treasury paid to borrow $13 billion on Wednesday was the highest yield at a 20-year auction since 1986. Discussion of whether the government should scrap this less liquid maturity altogether has intensified recently. Meanwhile, US federal debt has crossed the $40 trillion threshold, while Washington's interest bill for fiscal 2026 hit a record $1.36 trillion, putting interest payments as a share of GDP at a historic high of 3.2%. These metrics are all rising. When debt is above $40 trillion, a few basis points lower in borrowing costs can save billions. This points to an obvious strategy for lowering average government borrowing costs: lighten the load at the long end of the curve and borrow more at the front, where rates are lower. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent appears intent on doing just that. In August, Treasury announced it would at least double its $2 billion scheduled buybacks of longer-dated debt, referring to 10-year notes and 20- and 30-year bonds. It later increased that to $6 billion. Treasury said this reflected its "desire to provide greater liquidity support" to certain parts of the curve. That may be true, but it also just happens to align with longer-term efforts to shorten Treasury’s maturity profile. Around 22% of US public debt is currently in T-bills, which mature in one year or less, compared with around 15% five years ago. This is far from a “risk-free” strategy. By increasing the share of short-term debt, the government gives up the security of longer-term financing, meaning it must refinance more often. This "rollover risk" exposes the government to bouts of market shocks or volatility. But Bessent has few options. DEAR PRUDENCE A sudden burst of deficit-reduction fervor could sweep across Washington, leading to huge spending cuts or large tax hikes. But that's unlikely. The US budget deficit hit $2 trillion in fiscal 2026, more than 6% of GDP, and there is little appetite in the White House to tackle it. President Donald Trump recently pledged to mail $5,000 checks to every adult in the country if his Republican Party wins both houses of Congress in the midterm elections on November 3, a splurge that would cost over $1.1 trillion, according to the Committee for a Responsible Federal Budget. Absent serious belt-tightening, Treasury has to consider other measures to help lower long-term borrowing costs. One could be reducing sales of the 20-year bond or getting rid of it entirely. The 20-year is one of the least liquid parts of the yield curve, with a limited supply of natural buyers. That means the government often has to offer a slightly more attractive yield. Markets will find out more in the first week of November when Treasury unveils its quarterly refunding plans. What can we expect? Normally, very little. In the words of the Treasury itself, the debt auction process, calendar and issuance amounts should be “regular and predictable” to ensure smooth functioning of the world's largest and most important market. But these are not normal times. The Treasury’s $6 billion accelerated buyback plan proved to be a bit of a flop, as the government failed to purchase the full amount in the first two rounds of buybacks in September. More importantly, long-dated yields rose as much as 50 basis points following the buyback announcement. Citi's US rates strategists expect 20-year and 30-year auction sizes to be reduced by $3 billion, with the gap filled by additional bill issuance. Treasury may also opt for more flexibility by keeping auction sizes unchanged but signaling that future adjustments are in play. Alternatively, Treasury may decide to retain the status quo. Analysts at JPMorgan reckon the scale of borrowing required in the coming years is so huge that it would "not be prudent" to discontinue a "critical" source of funding from an instrument that raises $168 billion a year. What's more, yields might be high, but they're not disconnected from current economic fundamentals, they argue. Given that the midterm elections are also in the first week of November, Treasury’s quarterly refunding plan may not be absolutely top of mind for investors. But that might be a mistake, as subtle changes in the government’s funding strategy could have big implications down the line. (The opinions expressed here are those of the author, a columnist for Reuters) Enjoying this column? Check out Reuters Open Interest (ROI), your essential new source for global financial commentary. Follow ROI on LinkedIn, and X. And listen to the Morning Bid daily podcast on Apple, Spotify, or the Reuters app. Subscribe to hear Reuters journalists discuss the biggest news in markets and finance seven days a week.

item.title: Cricket-England's Brook hits record ODI double ton but Sri Lanka pull off epic chase
item.description: England's Harry Brook smashed the fastest double-century in One-Day International history and became the first Englishman to score 200 in the format but Sri Lanka sealed a two-wicket win in their tri-series clash with one ball to spare on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: England's Harry Brook smashed the fastest double-century in One-Day International history and became the first Englishman to score 200 in the format but Sri Lanka sealed a two-wicket win in their tri-series clash with one ball to spare on Thursday. The 27-year-old captain rewrote the record books by racing to his double hundred in 114 balls, surpassing the previous mark of 117 deliveries set by India's Shubman Gill. In the process, Brook also eclipsed England's highest individual ODI score of 182, held by all-rounder Ben Stokes. Brook's scintillating performance ended with the final ball of England's innings when he was caught by Sahan Arachchige off the bowling of Janith Liyanage. He made 202 from 116 deliveries, peppering the Sri Lanka attack with 21 fours and 10 sixes before departing to warm applause from the crowd. The defeat leaves England bottom of the standings after losing both their matches, with Brook saying they need to win their next two games to reach the final in Lahore. "Unfortunately, it (the record) doesn't matter now. I thought we were going to be in a good position but, unfortunately, it doesn't even count," Brook said. "Heart-breaking. I think you've hit the nail on the head there. It's very disappointing that we haven't been able to defend 430, but that's life, that's cricket," he added. "You don't see many teams chase down 430 and hats off to Sri Lanka. They've played exceptionally well. We couldn't execute our skills enough with the ball and, again, they've just played an absolute blinder there ... "We'll have a good chat about it now and over the next couple of days. We've got a good opportunity in the next couple of games to really try and get to that final in Lahore." Joe Root provided strong support with 69 off 66 balls as England piled up 429-4. But the total proved insufficient as Sri Lanka completed the second-highest successful run chase in ODI history. Pavan Rathnayake top-scored with 130 from 106 deliveries, while opener Avishka Fernando and Dasun Shanaka both fell three runs short of centuries. Needing six runs from the final two deliveries, Sri Lanka sealed victory when Liyanage launched Josh Tongue over long-off for six, leaving Brook's record-breaking innings all in vain. Tongue was England's most successful bowler with 3-79. England lost by 87 runs at the same venue in Rawalpindi on Tuesday to Pakistan, who lead the table with two wins from two.

item.title: Tesla drops as spending pullback clouds AI, robotics ambitions
item.description: Tesla’s shares slid five per cent in premarket trading on Thursday as the EV maker’s reduced capital spending forecast raised questions about the pace of investment behind Elon Musk’s AI, robotics and ...
item.dc:creator: Reuters Staff
item.content:encoded: Tesla’s shares slid five per cent in premarket trading on Thursday as the EV maker’s reduced capital spending forecast raised questions about the pace of investment behind Elon Musk’s AI, robotics and autonomous-driving ambitions. The company on Wednesday lowered its 2026 capital spending forecast to about US$20 billion from more than $25 billion after spending far less than expected on AI and robotics in the third quarter, which led to a surprise positive free cash flow. The strong position may prove valuable as CEO Musk explores combining Tesla with the far more capital-intensive SpaceX. But “investors are likely to come away with mixed feelings,” J.P.Morgan analysts, led by Rajat Gupta, wrote in a note. “The delay helps near-term cash burn but also suggests delays in investments that matter for fruition of long-term opportunities.” Wednesday’s management commentary suggested spending will be ramped up in 2027 and 2028 as Tesla continues to fund robotaxi, Optimus, AI compute and Terafab milestones, the brokerage said. Tesla’s shares have declined about 14 per cent this year, in contrast to the Nasdaq’s roughly 15 per cent gain. The stock is about 23 per cent below its record intraday high of $498.83, reached in December 2025. Its valuation, however, remains well above peers: Tesla traded at 188.24 times its forward earnings estimates, compared with 6.58 for Ford and 5.16 for General Motors. “The risk is Tesla now enters a period of limbo while investors await news on a potential combination with SpaceX, which ... might face significant regulatory hurdles,” said Russ Mould, investment director at AJ Bell. (Reporting by Joel Jose in Bengaluru; Editing by Joyjeet Das)

item.title: Rifts emerge in Libya as eastern parliament backs central bank chief's resignation
item.description: A new contest for control of the central bank in divided Libya could emerge after the eastern-based parliament said on Thursday it approved in principle the resignation of its governor, Naji Issa, and backed a member of the bank's board to replace him on an interim basis.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A new contest for control of the central bank in divided Libya could emerge after the eastern-based parliament said on Thursday it approved in principle the resignation of its governor, Naji Issa, and backed a member of the bank's board to replace him on an interim basis. The House of Representatives's (HoR) spokesperson said parliament backed Fowzi Musbah Abukhzam, the board member, to temporarily fill the role at the central bank. In the western half of the North African country, however, Naji Mukhtar Ali, the first deputy of the High Council of State (HCS), rejected Issa's resignation and told him to stay in his post. Yet the head of HCS, Mohamed Takala, contradicted his first deputy's position, and called on Abukhzam to carry on his duties on an interim basis, in line with the HoR decision, underlining some rifts even among the main Libyan factions. "You are requested to assume your duties and carry out the functions of the Governor of the Central Bank of Libya on an interim basis, pending an agreement with the House of Representatives on the appointment of a Governor for the Central Bank," Takala said in a letter to Abukhzam, which was viewed by Reuters and confirmed by a person at the HCS. The eastern parliament will discuss Issa's resignation in a coming session, its spokesperson wrote on X. In August, Issa submitted his resignation to the two legislative chambers, saying he could not continue in his post but without explaining why, according to two documents seen by Reuters at the time. DIVIDED COUNTRY Libya has been split since 2014 into rival authorities in the west and east that emerged from the turmoil following the fall of Muammar Gaddafi in a NATO-backed uprising in 2011. It is now run by the eastern-based HoR, which was elected in 2014, and the western-based HCS, whose members were drawn from a parliament elected in 2012. After Issa submitted his resignation, both chambers had said he should stay in the position until the issue was discussed. In reaction to Thursday's decision by the eastern parliament, Ali, the HCS first deputy in the west, rejected what he called "the unilateral measures taken by the presidency of the House of Representatives." "You are requested to continue performing your tasks," Ali told Issa in a letter seen by Reuters that was confirmed by a central bank official and an HCS source. Issa took up the post in 2024 when the two legislative chambers agreed on his appointment as a way to end a stand off over control of the central bank. Separately, the central bank said in a statement on its verified Facebook page that it condemned the forced entry of people into its headquarters, violating the governor’s office in his absence. It did not explain the incident, but it said it holds all those involved responsible for any consequences, "foremost among them the Ministry of Defence, given its responsibility for protecting and securing the bank’s headquarters." In a separate incident, masked men tried to [USN:L1N4670MR TEXT:"storm the country's financial oversight agency"] on Wednesday, in what Libya's UN mission called an "unacceptable" attempt to install a senior employee by force.

item.title: ＰＨＰ脆弱性、世界で修正急ぐ 攻撃試行は数百万件に
item.description:
Eduardo Baptista
[東京／北京／アムステルダム ２２日 ロイター] - 世界各国の企業や政府は２２日、...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
ＰＨＰ脆弱性、世界で修正急ぐ　攻撃試行は数百万件に 10/22 20:42 配信

英機関によるＰＨＰの脆弱性への警告、22日撮影 REUTERS/Toby Melville

Eduardo Baptista

[東京／北京／アムステルダム ２２日 ロイター] - 世界各国の企業や政府は２２日、広く利用されているプログラミング言語「ＰＨＰ」で見つかった重大な脆弱性の修正を急いだ。サイバーセキュリティー企業によると、脆弱性の公表後に確認されたハッキングの試みは数百万件に及ぶ。

前日の２１日には、ウェブサイト運営者がＰＨＰを使うシステムの安全確保に追われる中、欧州などの政府が予防措置としてウェブサイトを停止した。ＰＨＰの開発者は、人工知能（ＡＩ）によって発見されるまで何年も潜んでいた脆弱性の緊急修正プログラムを公開、利用者に「直ちに更新する」よう呼びかけた。

世界各国で銀行、航空、鉄道、税務、行政のサービスが緊急停止し、公共・企業システムのＰＨＰへの依存度の高さと、脆弱性が明らかになった後に迅速に修正する難しさを示した。

マイクロソフトのサティア・ナデラ最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）は２２日、ドイツのケルンで開いた同社のイベントで「ＩＴやセキュリティーに携わる全ての人にとって、長い一日、長い夜だったと思う。これほどの事態は長らく見たことがない」と語った。

今回の事態は、安全に保守が可能なデジタルシステム構築の重要性を浮き彫りにしたと述べた。

ベルギーのサイバーセキュリティー企業アイキドウ ・セキュリティーの共同創業者、マデリン・ローレンス氏は「修正プログラムの準備が整う前に脆弱性の詳細が公になり、攻撃が報告されている」と説明。「攻撃に備え企業は更新を急いでいる。まさに時間との競争だ」と語った。

クラウドサービス企業クラウドフレアとアマゾン・ドット・コムによると、企業や政府が修正プログラムを適用し、予防措置としてウェブサイトを停止する中、ハッキングの試みは数百万件に急増した。

クラウドフレアのマシュー・プリンスＣＥＯは２１日夜、「公表前の１０時間に、当社のネットワーク全体で脆弱性を悪用しようとする試みを数千件確認した」とＸに投稿。「公表後４５分で数万件、２時間以内に数十万件に跳ね上がり、今では数百万件に達している」とした。

アマゾンも、脆弱性が広く悪用されていることを確認したと述べた。

日本では野村ホールディングス、三菱ＵＦＪフィナンシャル・グループ、ＡＮＡホールディングス、ＪＲ東日本などが２２日、緊急措置の一環として一部のインターネットサービスを一時停止すると発表した。

東京海上ホールディングスは、グループ会社のウェブサイトを停止したと明らかにした。

財務省と気象庁は安全対策を実施するためオンラインサービスを一部停止し、国税庁もサービスを一時停止した。

予防的な停止措置は、日本でサイバーセキュリティーへの懸念が高まっていることを示している。トレンドＡＩのデータによると、２０２６年１─９月に日本で記録されたサイバーインシデントの件数は、２５年通年を上回った。

フランスの通信大手オレンジは、予防措置として、複数の子会社でＰＨＰを使う一部のウェブサイトやアプリケーションへのアクセスを一時停止したと説明した。

中国のクラウドサービス大手テンセントクラウドは、更新版のＰＨＰを導入するよう顧客に呼びかけたが、広範なウェブサイト停止を求めるには至らなかった。

フィンランドの政府ＩＴサービス機関バルトリは、前日に政府の一般向けウェブサービスを停止した後、夜間もＰＨＰのセキュリティー修正プログラムの適用を続け、予防的なサービス停止を段階的に解除していると説明した。「更新に加えてシステムを慎重にテストする必要があるため、サービスの復旧には数日、場合によっては数週間かかる可能性がある」と声明で述べた。

同機関は、サービス停止は脆弱性の悪用やサイバー侵害によるものではなく、脆弱性が実際に悪用された事例も把握していないと説明した。

＜修正に数週間かかる場合も＞

アジアの複数の政府は２２日、ＰＨＰの脆弱性に関連するサイバーセキュリティー点検を指示した。

中国の工業情報省は、組織や利用者にシステムを直ちに点検し、安全性が確保された最新のＰＨＰに更新するよう呼びかけた。また、サイバーセキュリティー監視を強化し、必要に応じてアカウント、パスワード、鍵（キー） を変更するよう勧告した。

韓国はハッキング攻撃のリスク増大への懸念を理由に、民間部門のサイバーセキュリティー警戒レベルを引き上げ、緊急対応措置を発動した。

ドイツのＩＴ・通信・ニューメディア産業連合会（ＢＩＴＫＯＭ）でセキュリティー部門を率いるフェリックス・クーレンカンプ氏は、大規模な運営事業者の多くは既に更新を済ませたものの、複雑なＩＴシステムや小規模な組織では、さらに時間がかかる可能性があると指摘。「ＰＨＰを使うウェブサイトを運営していても、その状況を十分に把握していない場合がある」とし、「セキュリティー更新が提供されていない古いバージョンのＰＨＰに基づくウェブサイトの場合、システム全体を更新しなければならない」と語った。

item.title: スポティファイ、予想上回る第4四半期営業益見込む ＡＩ機能で
item.description: [２２日 ロイター] - スウェーデンの音楽配信大手スポティファイは２２日、第４・四半期の営業利益が８億２０００万ユー...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
スポティファイ、予想上回る第4四半期営業益見込む　ＡＩ機能で 10/22 19:55 配信

スポティファイのロゴ、ニューヨーク証券取引所のフロアで2023年撮影 REUTERS/Brendan McDermid

[２２日 ロイター] - スウェーデンの音楽配信大手スポティファイは２２日、第４・四半期の営業利益が８億２０００万ユーロ（９億２０５３万ドル）になるとの見通しを示し、アナリスト予想の８億１３４０万ユーロを上回った。人工知能（ＡＩ）を活用した機能を背景に、ホリデーシーズンにおけるユーザー数の拡大を見込んでいる。

同社の株価はプレマーケット取引で３％以上上昇した。

スポティファイは、音声コメント付きのパーソナライズされた音楽ミックスをキュレートする「AI DJ」や、ユーザーが気分や好みの音楽を説明することで、それに合わせた選曲を生成するプロンプトベースのプレイリストなど、ＡＩを活用した機能を提供。ＡＩへの投資を進めているため、投資家は同社の収益性を注視している。

第３・四半期の営業利益は６億７２００万ユーロと、アナリスト予想の６億７１８０万ユーロとほぼ一致。売上高は４９億７０００万ユーロで、予想は４９億８０００万ユーロだった。

同社は、成長が持続的に加速する強固なビジネスを構築しているとして、「今後もさらなる成長の余地がある」と述べた。

第４・四半期における月間アクティブユーザー数（ＭＡＵ）見通しは８億１８００万人。市場予想の８億１９００万人をわずかに下回った一方、プレミアム加入者数が１０００万人増加して３億１６００万人に達するという見通しは、予想の３億１４７０万人を上回った。

item.title: 中国恒大集団の清算人、2年半で債権の回収1％どまり
item.description: [香港 ２２日 ロイター] - 破綻した中国不動産開発業者、中国恒大集団の清算人は２２日、２０２４年１月に香港の裁判所...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
中国恒大集団の清算人、2年半で債権の回収1％どまり 10/22 19:50 配信

中国恒大のロゴ、香港で2021年撮影 REUTERS/Tyrone Siu/File Photo

[香港 ２２日 ロイター] - 破綻した中国不動産開発業者、中国恒大集団の清算人は２２日、２０２４年１月に香港の裁判所が清算を命じて以来２回目となる進捗報告書を公表し、これまでの資産売却や貸付金回収を通じて４億３５９０万ドルを回収したと明らかにした。ただ、同社に対して約４６０億ドルの債権を保有する債権者への返済がいかに困難であるかが浮き彫りになっている。

清算人は、２７年上半期に債権者への第１回中間配当を目指すとしているが、その額は未定だ。

かつて中国最大の不動産開発業者だった同社は、約３０００億ドルの負債の大部分について債務不履行に陥り、中国不動産危機の象徴となった。

香港本社で発見された１０７点の美術品のうち９６点が２８８０万ドルで売却されたが、損失を伴うものだったという。このコレクションには、ピカソ、モネ、ウォーホルの作品に加え、ムーアやヘップワースの彫刻も含まれていた。

第４・四半期にはプライベートジェットも売却対象となっており、約１２００万ドルでの売却が見込まれている。また、清算人は、２０年に行われた寄付金の一部について、米国の大学に対し２００万ドルの返還を求めている。

業界の専門家らは、会社の規模と複雑さを考慮すると、恒大集団の清算が完了するまでには１０年以上かかる可能性があると指摘している。

item.title: ＰＨＰの脆弱性、韓国が緊急対応 サイバー警戒レベル引き上げ
item.description: [ソウル ２２日 ロイター] - 韓国政府は２２日、ウェブ開発用プログラミング言語「ＰＨＰ」に重大な脆弱性が見つかり、...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
ＰＨＰの脆弱性、韓国が緊急対応　サイバー警戒レベル引き上げ 10/22 19:33 配信

コンピュータサーバーのケーブル、ベルリンで21日撮影 REUTERS/Annegret Hilse

[ソウル ２２日 ロイター] - 韓国政府は２２日、ウェブ開発用プログラミング言語「ＰＨＰ」に重大な脆弱性が見つかり、ハッキングの危険性が高まったことを受け、民間部門のサイバーセキュリティー警戒レベルを引き上げ、緊急対応措置を発動した。

大統領府の発表によると、国家安保室は情報機関、国防省、科学省の当局者を集めた緊急会議を開き、官民と軍の対応を検討した。

科学省は、最高情報セキュリティー責任者を登録している約２万８０００社と、政府の情報共有ネットワークに参加する５９００のメンバーのほか、重要インフラの運営事業者、ウェブホスティング企業、データセンターにセキュリティー対策を通知したと明らかにした。

政府は各組織に対し、ＰＨＰの開発者が２１日に公開したセキュリティー更新プログラムを導入するよう促し、すぐに修正できない場合は暫定的な防御措置を講じるよう求めた。

科学省によると、これらの脆弱性が悪用されると、攻撃者が認証なしで悪意のあるコマンドを実行したり、データを盗んだり、ウェブサイトを停止させたりする恐れがある。

item.title: Republican backlash over Russia policy poses challenge for Trump in Congress
item.description: Bipartisan opposition potentially complicates Trump's agenda.
item.dc:creator: Richard Cowan
item.content:encoded: US President Donald Trump's moves in recent weeks to ease economic pressure on Russia while stepping up criticism of Ukraine have triggered bipartisan opposition in Congress, potentially complicating his agenda after next month's midterm elections. Seeking to draw Russian President Vladimir Putin into negotiations to end the war in Ukraine, Trump has [USN:L4N45Y0AR TEXT:"lifted sanctions on Russian diesel exports "]and [USN:FWN4622VQ TEXT:"waived newly enacted sanctions"] against Russian officials, oligarchs, banks and state enterprises. At the same time, he has increased pressure on Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy, calling for him to be replaced as the country's leader. A satellite system used by Ukraine for battlefield communications and drone operations was [USN:L1N4610ZC TEXT:"throttled"] following an order from inside the White House, Reuters reported last week. Seventeen Democrats and five Republicans in the House of Representatives urged Trump in an October 15 letter to "apply the Graham law's sanctions to their fullest extent and without delay." The lawmakers added that Putin "has repeatedly shown that he responds to pressure, not goodwill." They were referring to legislation, championed by the late Senator Lindsey Graham of South Carolina, that Congress passed overwhelmingly and Trump signed into law in mid-September. The Republican signatories were Representatives Brian Fitzpatrick of Pennsylvania, Joe Wilson of South Carolina, Michael McCaul of Texas, Don Bacon of Nebraska and Dan Newhouse of Washington state. The backlash could pose new hurdles for Trump after the November 3 midterm elections, when Congress takes up defense and spending bills that lawmakers could use to try to reverse or alter his Russia policies. Fitzpatrick went further. In a post on X on Monday he wrote that any move to [USN:L1N464034 TEXT:"limit the use of "Starshield""] intelligence to warn Kyiv of Russian attacks would be "fully investigated" by Congress with "harsh and punitive budget cuts to any responsible agency or agency head." The White House pushed back in an email to Reuters: “President Trump has been clear that he wants to see this brutal war come to an end," White House spokeswoman Taylor Rogers said, adding that Trump "retains the ability to exercise these authorities at any time if he determines that doing so would advance national interests." PROSPECT OF BIPARTISAN OPPOSITION TO TRUMP'S PRIORITIES The pushback has raised the possibility that some Republican lawmakers could join Democrats in investigations and legislation reversing Trump's priorities following the midterm elections. Congress' post-election work includes attempts to pass a bill authorizing defense programs for another year and across-the-board government spending through September 30, 2027, that includes appropriations for the Pentagon and intelligence agencies. If Congress uses those bills to try to change his Russia policies, Trump could veto them, setting up a showdown. James Lindsay, a US foreign policy expert at the Council on Foreign Relations, said the Republican backlash was not surprising given the Senate's bipartisan votes on the Graham bill. But passing legislation faces major challenges, Lindsay said. "Even if Congress can overcome its institutional divisions, its partisan divisions and overcome a presidential veto ... that's no guarantee the president will act or observe that constraint," he said. REPUBLICANS BACKING TRUMP Despite the growing pushback, many Republicans are backing Trump. Republican Senator Ted Budd told Reuters at a Trump rally in his home state of North Carolina that he supports the president's pivot toward Putin, saying the recent agreement on Russian diesel sales was important to keep Moscow involved in negotiations to end its war with Ukraine. "It's a very minimal dollar amount actually to Russia, but it's enough of a fig leaf to get them to the table to bring an end to the aggression against Ukraine," said Budd, an Armed Services Committee member. The elections, which will determine whether Republicans hold their narrow House and Senate majorities, could influence the way legislative battles between the two parties, and with Trump, turn out. Trump is not on the ballot, but the elections are widely seen as a referendum on his presidency. Voters are on edge over rising consumer prices and the war with Iran. An [USN:L1N45Z0TJ TEXT:"October 13 letter"] to Trump signed by five senior Senate Republicans, along with six Democrats, also criticized his diesel agreement. House Speaker Mike Johnson, a staunch supporter of Trump, has even hinted at his discomfort with current Russia policy. Asked on Fox News' Sunday Morning Futures program whether he supported Trump's decision to waive the Russia sanctions, Johnson said: "Congress voted on this decisively." He added that he was in discussions with Republican members of the Foreign Affairs and Intelligence committees. "We understand that Putin cannot be trusted," Johnson said and added that he told White House officials: "We need to talk about it and I think carefully consider the unintended consequences that may ensue" from putting the new Russia sanctions on hold.

item.title: ロシュ、第3四半期売上高が予想上回る 主力薬堅調
item.description:
Patrick Wingrove Marleen Kaesebier
[チューリヒ／ロンドン ２２日] - スイスの製...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
ロシュ、第3四半期売上高が予想上回る　主力薬堅調 10/22 19:04 配信

スイスの製薬大手ロシュのロゴ。2018年2月1日、スイスのバーゼルで撮影。 REUTERS/Arnd Wiegmann

Patrick Wingrove　Marleen Kaesebier

[チューリヒ／ロンドン ２２日] - スイスの製薬大手ロシュが２２日発表した第３・四半期売上高は、市場予想を上回った。「オクレバス」など主力薬の需要が堅調だった。

グループ売上高は為替変動の影響を除くベースで７％増の１６１億３０００万スイスフラン（１９６億１０００万ドル）となり、同社がまとめた市場予想の１５７億５０００万フラン（１９１億５０００万ドル）を上回った。

ただ競争圧力の兆しも表れた。大型薬「ゾレア」は初の安価な後続品が発売された影響で、売上高が８億４８００万フラン（１０億３０００万ドル）と、市場予想の９億２５００万フラン（１１億２０００万ドル）を下回った。

株価は午前の取引で１．１％下落した。

診断部門の売上高は５％増の３５億４０００万フラン（４３億ドル）で、経営陣は、来年は１桁台半ばから後半の「通常」の伸びに戻る見通しだとした。中国市場について、医療価格改革による下押し圧力は和らいでいると指摘した。

ドルの対スイスフラン相場が安定しつつあることもロシュに追い風となった。グループ売上高の半分近くを占める北米市場で、長引いていた為替の悪影響が和らいだ。

医薬品部門は主力薬がけん引した。中でも多発性硬化症の注射薬オクレバスは、売上高が為替変動の影響を除くベースで９％増の１８億４０００万フラン（２２億４０００万ドル）となった。

ロイター 関連ニュース コラム：米中間選挙目前、ドル円の行方を読む＝高島修氏 アングル：ロシア、欧州企業への圧力強化、米企業は優遇 アングル：接戦のテキサス上院選は民主に勝機、共和が大量資金投入でてこ入れ アングル：期待と誤算に揺れた日中の1年　高市政権下の改善「難しい」と関係者 アングル：金価格、米国債利回り上昇でも4000ドル台維持　中銀の準備資産分散が下支え 最終更新: 10/22(木) 19:04 ロイター

item.title: Musk's political baggage clouds prospects for SpaceX-Tesla deal
item.description: The possible merger may face bigger obstacles from politics than from regulation, drawing scrutiny in Beijing and potentially igniting a battle between President Donald Trump and the Democrats.
item.dc:creator: Cassell Bryan-Low, Hyunjoo Jin
item.content:encoded: A possible merger between Elon Musk's rocket company SpaceX (SPCX.O) and carmaker Tesla (TSLA.O) may face bigger obstacles from politics than from regulation, drawing scrutiny in Beijing and potentially igniting a battle between US President Donald Trump and the Democrats. Musk revived speculation about [USN:L4N4661IU TEXT:"a tie-up"] this week, calling a combination "a good idea" and confirming that committees at both companies were reviewing a potential deal, a step toward what could become the largest merger in history and create a company worth about $3.5 trillion. But a merger would also unite one of the US government's most important aerospace and defense contractors with one of the most China-exposed major American manufacturers — a combination likely to raise questions about national security risks both in Washington and in Beijing. Those concerns are unlikely to derail a deal, analysts said, but they would likely leave the combined company exposed to years of political wrangling and pressure from both sides of the Pacific. Tesla's China operations, they said, could become a source of leverage for Beijing in any future dispute with Washington, while a Democratic takeover of the US House of Representatives in next month's midterm elections could subject the deal to congressional investigations and political maneuvering. Democrats immediately raised concerns about the deal's implications, signaling their intent to turn the merger into a political flashpoint ahead of the November 3 midterms. “If Elon Musk moves forward with the merger of Tesla and SpaceX, the deal would carry real risks that antitrust enforcers across the world would scrutinize," said US Senator Cory Booker, a New Jersey Democrat who sits on both the Judiciary and Foreign Relations committees. He added that he was prepared to conduct oversight of any deal: "When one person controls the infrastructure that governments and militaries depend on, his business decisions become national security decisions, too." Musk could seek to address concerns by limiting how closely the two companies are integrated. The greater threat to the deal may come later, however, if a future administration takes a harder line on the relationship between Tesla and a company increasingly tied to US national security, analysts said. "A merger agreement would involve pledges of limits to the connections between SpaceX and Tesla," said Derek Scissors, a senior fellow at the American Enterprise Institute. "I don't think the Trump administration would enforce these limits. However, the next administration could certainly begin to scrutinize a merged entity. This may be the biggest risk to a deal - that it could get unwound in 2029." EXPOSURE TO CHINA For Beijing, a merger would effectively place Tesla's sprawling Shanghai manufacturing hub under the same corporate umbrella as SpaceX, a company that has become deeply embedded in US military and national security activities through its Pentagon work and through Starlink's role in conflicts, including Ukraine. "A formal merger would make it harder for Chinese authorities to treat Tesla as a purely commercial actor, raising risks for future factory expansions, data approvals, or market access," said Alicia Garcia-Herrero, a senior research fellow at the Brussels-based Bruegel think tank. Tesla's reliance on production from Shanghai already gives China considerable leverage over Musk's business empire. A merger could extend that control to a broader corporate group encompassing strategically important assets such as satellite communications, launch services and military-related technologies. GLOBAL REGULATORY HURDLES The deal would also have to navigate a maze of reviews around the world as competition authorities assess its impact on industries ranging from automobiles and satellite communications to artificial intelligence and semiconductors. Musk's close relationship with Trump would likely dispel concerns about potential US regulatory roadblocks to a transaction, analysts said, while antitrust experts see limited competition concerns because the companies operate largely in separate markets. Outside the United States, however, foreign regulators are likely to scrutinize whether a combined company would gain an unfair advantage by integrating technologies spanning automobiles, artificial intelligence and aerospace. Antitrust experts said authorities in markets with powerful domestic auto industries, such as China and South Korea, could examine whether Tesla's access to SpaceX technologies would give it an advantage that rivals cannot replicate, creating barriers for competitors and potentially undermining domestic manufacturers. Regulators could respond by requiring the company to license key technologies to competitors as part of any approval, said Ioannis Kokkoris, a law professor at Queen Mary University of London. A South Korean antitrust official told Reuters that the merger, if pursued, could require an in-depth review of its potential impact on that country's industries. "Korean antitrust officials will be wary of the merger. They will take the merger very seriously," said Lee Hwang, a law professor at Korea University and former Korea Fair Trade Commission official. "The stakes are very high in Korea because it regards both the automotive and aerospace sectors as strategically important industries."

item.title: 中国・香港株式市場・大引け＝ＡＩ関連主導で下落、ＣＳＩ３００弱気相場入り
item.description: [上海／香港 ２２日 ロイター] - 中国・香港株式市場は下落。中国の主要株価指数ＣＳＩ３００指数は１５カ月ぶりの安値と...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
中国・香港株式市場・大引け＝ＡＩ関連主導で下落、ＣＳＩ３００弱気相場入り 10/22 18:55 配信

[上海／香港 ２２日 ロイター] - 中国・香港株式市場は下落。中国の主要株価指数ＣＳＩ３００指数は１５カ月ぶりの安値となり弱気相場入りが確認された。人工知能（ＡＩ）関連株が、成長とバリュエーションの持続性に対する懸念から急落したことが背景。

ＣＳＩ３００指数は１．８％下落し、４０３６．３０で終了。２０２５年７月以来の安値となった。６月２２日に付けた終値ベースの直近高値から２０．２％下落し、弱気相場の目安とされる２０％下落の水準を超えた。

終値ベースでは、同指数は２００７年に付けた高値を更新しておらず、６月に相場を５年ぶりの高値に押し上げた勢いはその後急速に反転した。

香港のロータス・アセット・マネジメントのマネジングパートナー兼最高投資責任者（ＣＩＯ）、ハオ・ホン氏は「市場は底なしの状況だ」と述べた。

上海総合指数は１．５％下落して終了し１年超ぶりの安値となった。

アジア全域のハイテク主力株に広がった売り、低調な景気刺激策への期待、新たな材料の欠如を背景に、中国市場で広範な売りが加速した。

上昇したのは生活必需品指数と公益事業指数のみ。

ホン氏は「国家隊はためらっている」とし、売り局面でしばしば介入する中国の国有投資ファンドに言及した。

ＣＳＩ半導体指数は３．６％下落、ＣＳＩ人工知能指数は３．３％下落した。深セン証券取引所の新興企業向け市場「創業板（チャイネクスト）」総合指数は４．４％急落し、２５年７月以来の安値を付けた。

トレーダーやアナリストによると、中国政府の小出しの景気刺激策への失望も市場心理の重しとなっている。また、第３・四半期の経済成長率が予想を上回ったことで、追加の政策支援への期待が後退した。

＜課税問題が重しとなる香港市場＞

香港市場では、ハンセン指数が３％下落し、４カ月ぶりの安値を付けた。ハンセンテック指数は５％下落し、２年ぶりの安値となった。

一部の投資家は、香港上場の中国企業の株主の多くが採用している一般的な仕組みであるオフショア信託に対し、中国政府が所得税の徴収を進める取り組みを、売り圧力のもう一つの要因として指摘した。

ロータスのホン氏は、きょうが税申告の最終日だと指摘。過去数週間の売りは、中国企業の創業者らが主導したとし「納税義務を果たすための現金を調達するため、資産を売却していたのは明らかだ」と述べた。

２２日の下落が大きかった銘柄では、テンセントが２．９％下落、アリババが６％超急落した。

盛期資本（香港）のゼン・ウェンカイＣＩＯは「これほど急激かつ急速な下落は非常にまれで、特にテンセントのような主力銘柄ではなおさらだ。これはおそらくパニック売りの最終局面で、市場の売りは終わりに近づいている」と説明。「ただ、これほどの傷からの回復には時間がかかるだろう」と語った。

ロイター 関連ニュース アングル：ＡＩ関連の資金調達、低格付け領域にも拡大　投資家は警戒感強める コラム：ベセント氏の危うい賭け、ＡＩ主導の経済成長は「債務病」の特効薬ならず コラム：ＩＴサービス企業、生成ＡＩ追い風に株価上昇か コラム：ＡＩ投資を「黄金」に変えたマイクロソフト、アルファベットは羨望か コラム：米アップル、ＥＶ断念でもＡＩによる収益化期待揺るがず 最終更新: 10/22(木) 18:58 ロイター

item.title: S&P 500, Nasdaq end sharply lower as revived AI doubts ignite tech selloff
item.description: US stocks tumbled on Thursday and the Nasdaq posted its steepest daily drop since early June as a batch of high-profile earnings reports ignited fresh fears about the AI spending race.
item.dc:creator: Stephen Culp, Tharuniyaa Lakshmi
item.content:encoded: US stocks tumbled on Thursday and the Nasdaq posted its steepest daily drop since early June as a batch of high-profile earnings reports ignited fresh fears about the AI spending race. The S&P 500 ended deep in negative territory. But the tech-laden Nasdaq, dragged down by microchips, suffered a steeper loss, falling 2.6% in the wake of a spate of high-profile AI-related earnings results. The blue-chip Dow eked out a nominal gain minutes before the closing bell. [USN:L4N4671S3 TEXT:"Meta Platforms"]' (META.O) results beat analyst expectations, but its stock slid 7.0% as the Facebook parent posted its first cash outflow in more than a decade due to its AI-related expenditures and announced plans to issue non-voting shares in a two-for-one split to raise capital to spend on the nascent technology. [USN:L4N4671SD TEXT:"Tesla"] (TSLA.O) shares fell 3.1% even though the electric car maker unexpectedly posted positive free cash flow in the quarter and cut its 2026 capital spending plans. The Philadelphia SE Semiconductor Index (.SOX) , which has driven much of the current bull market's gains, plunged 6.7%, its biggest daily percentage drop since June 23. With Thursday's decline, the SOX is off more than 26% from its record closing high reached on June 22, yet it remains up 51.5% so far this year. The S&P 500 has risen 11.9% over the same period. "It's a wonderful day on Wall Street," said Paul Nolte, senior wealth adviser & market strategist at Murphy & Sylvest in Elmhurst, Illinois. "The only part of the market that is really suffering here is technology, which has been the golden child of the markets up until about June." "Investors are starting to realize that there are some holes in the AI story," Nolte added. "And that's having an impact on the indices because they're so heavily weighted toward technology." On the geopolitical stage, Iran-backed Houthis launched new strikes against Saudi targets, sending [USN:L1N46801N TEXT:"crude prices"] to a five-month high. Investors worried that ongoing Middle East strife could keep inflation hot and force the US Federal Reserve to keep raising interest rates. Data from the Labor Department showed [USN:L1N4680T1 TEXT:"initial claims for unemployment"] benefits kept drifting along near multi-decade lows. Signs of labor market stability will allow the Fed to focus on fighting inflation. Financial markets are currently pricing in the probability that the central bank will raise its policy rate by another 25 basis points before year-end. The Dow Jones Industrial Average (.DJI) rose 11.89 points, or 0.02%, to 52,867.98, the S&P 500 (.SPX) lost 93.74 points, or 1.21%, to 7,663.43 and the Nasdaq Composite (.IXIC) lost 694.00 points, or 2.60%, to 26,008.86. Third-quarter earnings season is well underway, with 111 of the companies in the S&P 500 having reported. Of those, 83% have beaten analyst expectations, according to the most recent LSEG data. [USN:L4N46811U TEXT:"Procter & Gamble"] (PG.N) warned that rising cost pressures would take an increasing bite out of profit, but beat analyst estimates, sending the stock 5.6% higher and supporting consumer staples (.SPLRCS) . [USN:L4N4681XJ TEXT:"Blackstone"] (BX.N) advanced 8.4%, after the company said widening credit spreads on AI-related debt could present an opportunity to lock in higher returns. [USN:L4N4680XC TEXT:"Lockheed Martin"] (LMT.N) climbed 7.0% after the aerospace/defense firm raised its annual sales and profit forecast. [USN:L4N4680UE TEXT:"Spotify"] (SPOT.N) rose 11.1% after the Swedish music streaming firm forecast fourth-quarter profit above Wall Street estimates, betting on its AI-powered features to drive user growth. [USN:L4N46817V TEXT:"Union Pacific"] (UNP.N) gained 3.6% following the company's quarterly earnings beat, which was helped by core pricing gains, although the railroad flagged a hit from rising fuel prices. Chipmakers Intel (INTC.O) , AMD (AMD.O) , Sandisk (SNDK.O) and Marvell (MRVL.O) all tumbled more than 8% amid the broader semiconductor selloff. Advancing issues outnumbered decliners by a 1.01-to-1 ratio on the NYSE. There were 173 new highs and 366 new lows on the NYSE. On the Nasdaq, 2,022 stocks rose and 2,766 fell as declining issues outnumbered advancers by a 1.37-to-1 ratio. The S&P 500 posted 40 new 52-week highs and four new lows while the Nasdaq Composite recorded 82 new highs and 342 new lows. Volume on US exchanges was 18.79 billion shares, compared with the 17.19 billion average for the full session over the last 20 trading days.

item.title: 再送-〔マクロスコープ〕27年春闘、芳野会長「底上げ余地まだ」 専門家は5％の着地予想
item.description:
(２２日１８：３３に配信した記事です)
Kentaro Sugiyama Makiko Yamazaki
［東京 ２...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
再送-〔マクロスコープ〕27年春闘、芳野会長「底上げ余地まだ」　専門家は5％の着地予想 10/22 18:38 配信

2026年6月16日、都内を歩く人々。REUTERS/Kim Kyung-Hoon

(２２日１８：３３に配信した記事です)

Kentaro Sugiyama　Makiko Yamazaki

［東京　２２日　ロイター］ - ２０２７年春闘の基本構想で連合は賃上げ率（定期昇給込み）を「６％中心、５％以上」とし、従来より高い数値目標を設定した。これまで３年連続で５％超の賃上げを実現してきたが、芳野友子会長は全体の底上げが足りないと主張する。一方、賃金情勢に詳しいエコノミストの間では５％前後で着地するとの見方が多い。

連合は２２日、「６％中心、５％以上」とする基本構想を発表した。過去３年にわたり目標に掲げた「５％以上」を実現してきたことを踏まえ、より高い目標を設定する必要があると判断した。一方、目標達成に至っていない産業別組織や単組は、引き続き５％以上が目標になるとした。

連合は２４年春闘で「５％以上」を賃上げ目標の目安とし、２５年は「その実現を目指す」、２６年は「その実現にこだわる」と段階的に表現を強めてきた。

妥結結果は２４年が５．１０％、２５年が５．２５％、２６年が５．０１％と３年連続で５％台を確保したが、企業規模間や産業別の格差が課題となっている。２７年も大企業・製造業が相場形成をけん引する構図は続くとみられる中、中小企業や非製造業への賃上げの波及が焦点となる。

同日会見した芳野会長は「５％以上の賃上げ率となった加盟組合の比率はいまだ５割に届いていない。全体の底上げの余地は、まだまだある」と語った。

連合の基本構想では、単年度の賃上げ目標に加え、２０３０年をめどに現行水準から１５％程度引き上げる中期目標も新たに設定した。

海外主要国で賃金が年１─２％ずつ上昇していることを踏まえ、「少なくとも日本全体の実質賃金の改善スピードを１％以上で維持」しつつ、中期的に日本全体の生産性を引き上げることでさらに加速する必要があると指摘した。

実際の賃上げ率は例年、要求水準を下回る。連合は６％を中心水準として掲げたが、民間エコノミストの間では５％前後で着地するとの見方が多い。

伊藤忠総研の高野蒼太・副主任研究員は、構造的な人手不足が続く中、賃上げ率が大きく下振れするリスクは高くないと指摘。ただ、昨年に比べて物価上昇率が鈍化していることなどから「４％台後半に着地する可能性が高い」と話す。

みずほ総合研究所の服部直樹チーフ日本経済エコノミストは、２７年の賃上げ率を定昇込みで５％ちょうどと予想する。企業収益や雇用環境を踏まえれば、５％前後の賃上げは十分実現可能だとみる。

日銀は持続的・安定的な２％の物価目標実現に向け、賃金と物価の好循環を重視している。連合は年内に正式な２７年春闘方針を決定し、その後、各産業別組織や単組が要求内容をまとめる。２７年の春闘の動向は、今後の金融政策運営を占う上でも重要な材料となる。

item.title: US banks are blocking third-party AI agents access to customer accounts, sources say
item.description: The industry has become increasingly concerned that sophisticated AI agents could harm the banking system and the institutions trusted to hold people's wealth.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Major US banks have been blocking third-party AI agents from operating inside customer accounts and making transactions, two people familiar with the situation said, following a report that AI agents were accessing bank accounts and taking actions independent of user instructions. The banking industry has become increasingly concerned that sophisticated AI agents could harm the banking system and the institutions trusted to hold people's wealth. An Axios report on Thursday said some AI agents attempted to take actions that appeared to be independent of user instructions, citing people familiar with the matter. In some cases, bank customers have shared their login ID and password with agents, with banks typically flagging and blocking those transactions, a person in the banking industry said. Still, such transactions cannot be deemed unauthorized if credentials were shared by the customer. Morgan Stanley (MS.N) has blocked third-party agents from accessing its platforms, but it had not seen any instances of unauthorized or rogue AI agents, according to a person familiar with the matter. Top banking executives earlier this month [USN:L4N45Z1M8 TEXT:"discussed the risks of AI agents"] acting on customers' behalf, with some warning the technology is adding significant risks for both customers and banks. JPMorgan Chase (JPM.N) CEO Jamie Dimon earlier this month said the largest US lender was developing tools to navigate the risk of AI agents carrying out tasks on their own. "We're not going to allow just any outside agent to come in inside the company because that's just too risky for clients and for JPMorgan," he said at the time. Charles Schwab (SCHW.N) CEO Richard Wurster earlier this month also said the brokerage was blocking unauthorized agents. "I get a report every day tracking how many times we've had to block one of the different agents, and it's not many because I think people aren't using it in that way in their financial life. We are blocking it because we want to have control over authentication and the experience," Wurster said.

item.description: [北京 ２２日 ロイター] - 中国商務省は２２日、１─９月の対内投資額は前年同期比４．３％減の５４８８億元（８２２...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
中国の対内投資額、1─9月は前年比4.3％減 10/22 18:16 配信

2025年11月4日、上海の夜景。REUTERS/Maxim Shemetov

[北京 ２２日 ロイター] - 中国商務省は２２日、１─９月の対内投資額は前年同期比４．３％減の５４８８億元（８２２億ドル）となった一方、非金融分野の対外直接投資額は計１０１０億ドルに達したと発表した。

対内投資の減少ペースは１─８月の５．３％から鈍化した。

商務次官は記者会見で、地政学的対立の激化、成長の勢いの鈍化、保護主義的・単独行動主義的な措置の増加など、中国が外資誘致で逆風に直面していると述べた。

一方、明るい材料としてハイテク産業を挙げ、１─９月の同分野への外国投資が３３．８％急増したと指摘。研究・開発・設計サービスがけん引した。

item.title: Musk’s public endorsement of SpaceX-Tesla deal may throw a wrench in talks
item.description: Elon Musk's public endorsement of a potential $3.5 trillion merger has rattled some insiders involved in the discussions, who worry his comments could invite shareholder scrutiny and delay the process by several weeks.
item.dc:creator: Milana Vinn
item.content:encoded: Elon Musk's [USN:L4N4661IU TEXT:"public endorsement"] this week of a potential $3.5 trillion merger between SpaceX (SPCX.O) and Tesla (TSLA.O) has rattled some insiders involved in the discussions, who worry his comments could invite shareholder scrutiny and delay the process by several weeks, according to a person with direct knowledge of the talks. The disclosure created a "mess" for the process, as it could lead to questions about how well Tesla shareholders' interests would be represented, the person said. The concerns reflect similarities some participants see with Tesla's 2016 acquisition of SolarCity, which sparked years of litigation over Musk's role in the deal. Musk, who serves as CEO of both SpaceX and Tesla and owns significant stakes in each company, this week told investors that the two companies were examining what would be the largest corporate transaction in history and revealed that both had formed special committees to evaluate it. The backlash to those remarks is reported here for the first time. The parties have hired advisers, but discussions are at an early stage, three sources familiar with the matter said. SpaceX approached Tesla in recent weeks, and the companies have been discussing a range of transaction structures, including a SpaceX acquisition of Tesla or a merger under a newly formed holding company, the person familiar with the matter said. They are weighing different forms of merger consideration, including an all-stock deal, the person said. These details of the talks have not been previously reported. Tesla, SpaceX and Musk did not respond to requests for comment. SHAREHOLDER LITIGATION OVER TESLA'S SOLARCITY DEAL In related-party transactions such as a SpaceX-Tesla merger, independent board members typically oversee the process to safeguard public shareholders' interests. That issue loomed large in Tesla's 2016 acquisition of SolarCity, which triggered [USN:L1N36V3J9 TEXT:"years of litigation"] after shareholders alleged the world's richest man had influenced the process to bail out his investment in the struggling rooftop solar company. At the time, Musk owned roughly 22% of both Tesla and SolarCity, which was founded by his cousins. Shareholders argued that Musk's involvement and public support undermined the deal's fairness. Central to the case were [USN:L2N2OL1K9 TEXT:"claims that despite his minority stake"], Musk was a controlling shareholder of Tesla due to his ties to board members and domineering style. The Delaware Supreme Court later noted that plaintiffs' contention of the absence of an independent committee, together with "certain other facts concerning Musk's involvement in and public support for the transaction," warranted the finding of unfair dealing. The courts ultimately upheld the acquisition as fair, though it took several years for the case to be resolved and Tesla directors settled allegations for $60 million. MUSK CANNOT BE INVOLVED IN TALKS Musk owns nearly a fifth of Tesla and just under half of SpaceX, and analysts have said a merger would give him control of the combined entity. On Tuesday's call with investors, Musk acknowledged that as a conflicted party he cannot be part of the discussions of the special committees. Advisers are also in contact with his lawyers to ensure Musk is recused from the merger discussions, the source familiar with the talks said. Eric Talley, a law professor at Columbia University, said a merger could benefit shareholders by eliminating the need for Musk to divide his time between the two companies. He added that any legal challenge may be harder to predict than the SolarCity case because Tesla is now incorporated in Texas rather than Delaware. “The Texas thing is a wild card. No one knows how Texas deals with cases like this because Texas never dealt with cases like this,” Talley said, noting that Texas has sought to establish itself as a business-friendly alternative to Delaware, and Musk’s comments so far were not necessarily problematic. Ultimately, he said, litigation risk would hinge on the terms of any transaction. "Who's going to get the better side of this deal? And that's usually what gives rise to litigation," Talley said. MUSK'S COMMENTS COULD AFFECT DISCUSSIONS People involved in the process worry Musk's public endorsement of the merger and disclosure of talks could intensify investor scrutiny, as interested parties typically avoid expressing views publicly while independent directors evaluate a deal, the source said. The SolarCity case could become a reference point for investors and courts assessing any future SpaceX-Tesla transaction if advisers fail to fully insulate the special committees from Musk's influence, the source added. A tie-up between Tesla and SpaceX would be the biggest deal in history, creating one of the world's largest industrial and technology groups. It would surpass Musk's acquisition earlier this year of his artificial intelligence company xAI by SpaceX, which ranks among the largest corporate transactions ever announced. A deal of this size would also face scrutiny from global regulators, especially due to Tesla’s business in China and SpaceX’s work in US defense and AI.

JERUSALEM: The US State Department has ordered some diplomats and family members to depart from its missions in Saudi Arabia and plans to withdraw family members from a number of other US missions in the region, US officials told Reuters. The order came as attacks in Saudi Arabia killed at least one person and injured eight others at a civilian airport in Dammam and two people were killed in a drone attack on an oil field. State Department spokesperson Tommy Pigott said in a post on X that the department ordered the departure of "non-emergency US government employees and their family members in Saudi Arabia only" amid attacks by the Iran-aligned Houthis in Yemen on civilian targets in the country. Washington had returned some diplomatic personnel to the region in recent months after many were pulled out when Tehran launched attacks on US facilities after the US-Israeli war on Iran began in late February.

"Iranian-supported Houthis have increasingly engaged in hostilities against Saudi Arabia, including attacks on civilian airports and other critical infrastructure resulting in civilian casualties and severe travel disruptions," Pigott said.

Related:

UK to deploy fighter jets to help protect Saudi from Houthi attacks

Singaporeans advised to defer all travel to Saudi Arabia amid heightened security risks: MFA

Four US officials told Reuters that US missions in other Gulf states would also be ordering family members to leave. Pigott did not address changes to other missions outside Saudi Arabia. The latest withdrawals follow an escalation of the fighting in Yemen, opening another front in the regional conflict triggered by the US-Israeli war on Iran. The wider conflict has snarled global energy trade and hurt Gulf economies. After the departure order, Saudi Arabia's civil aviation authority reported an attack on King Fahd International Airport in Dammam that killed one person and injured eight others. Earlier in the day, two people were killed after Saudi air defences intercepted a drone that was attempting to hit a facility at Saudi Aramco's Shaybah oilfield, the energy ministry said. The US embassy in Riyadh issued a security alert on Wednesday (Oct 21) about possible further attacks by the Houthis on Saudi Arabia, after recent deadly strikes including on Riyadh's airport. The embassy and a CIA station hosted there came under attack by drones in early March, as Iran began launching attacks across the region.

item.description: Cloud services firm Cloudflare saw millions of exploitation attempts after the public disclosure of critical vulnerabilities in the widely used programming language PHP, CEO Matthew Prince said in a post on X late on Wedn
item.dc:creator: CNA
item.content:encoded:

Cloudflare sees millions of exploit attempts after PHP disclosure

The logo of digital security firm Cloudflare is displayed over a booth at the Web Summit digital trade show in Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada, May 12, 2026. REUTERS/Chris Helgren

22 Oct 2026 12:10PM (Updated: 22 Oct 2026 01:21PM)

FAST

Cloud services firm Cloudflare saw millions of exploitation attempts after the public disclosure of critical vulnerabilities in the widely used programming language PHP , CEO Matthew Prince said in a post on X late on Wednesday.  "In the 10 hours before it was publicly announced, across the network we saw thousands of attempts to exploit it. That jumped to tens of thousands in the 45 minutes post announcement, hundreds of thousands within 2 hours, and millions now," Prince said.  Government websites in Europe and elsewhere went offline on Wednesday after the disclosure of vulnerabilities in PHP sent website operators around the world scrambling to protect their systems. Japanese lender Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group said it was temporarily suspending some internet services due to emergency measures.  Developers of the PHP programming language on Wednesday released urgent new fixes to vulnerabilities that had been lurking in their software for years until they were uncovered using AI, saying all users were "encouraged to update immediately." Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi also urged website owners on Wednesday to check whether their sites use PHP and prepare to apply the new fix.  Japan's Finance Ministry also temporarily suspended some website content and services while security measures were being implemented.

item.title: Hacking attempts surge as companies, governments rush to patch PHP flaws
item.description: Global firms and governments rushed to patch critical flaws in the PHP programming language that underpins much of the internet, as a cloud firm reported millions of hacking attempts after vulnerabilities were disclosed.
item.dc:creator: Eduardo Baptista, Toby Sterling, Mariko Katsumura
item.content:encoded: Global firms and governments rushed on Thursday to patch critical flaws in the [USN:L6N467127 TEXT:"PHP"] programming language that underpins much of the internet, as cloud firms reported a surge of hacking attempts after the vulnerabilities were disclosed. The push came after governments in Europe and elsewhere took websites [USN:L6N4670DM TEXT:"offline"] as a precaution on Wednesday while website operators scrambled to secure systems running the software. The emergency shutdowns of banking, airline, rail, tax and government services from Tokyo to [USN:L6N467188 TEXT:"Helsinki"] mark one of the most dramatic tests of the decades-old programming tools that keep the web running, exposing how deeply governments and companies depend on code that few people understand. "I've not seen anything like this in a long, long time," Microsoft (MSFT.O) CEO Satya Nadella said at an event in Germany on Thursday, saying the incident showed the importance of building software that can be maintained securely as systems grow more complex. "It was a long day and a long night, I know, for all the IT and security folks." PHP KEY TO INTERNET'S FOUNDATIONS LIKE HTML, PYTHON The developers of PHP - a computing language like HTML and Python - released [USN:L6N4670ZW TEXT:"fixes"] on Wednesday for vulnerabilities that had lurked in the software for years until they were uncovered using AI. They urged users to "update immediately". Madeline Lawrence, co-founder of Belgian cybersecurity firm Aikido Security, said that details of the flaws had become public before fixes were ready, with attacks reported since. "Companies are racing to update against attackers who can use AI to exploit them. That's the whole race," she said. As companies and governments deployed patches and suspended websites as a precaution, hacking attempts surged into the millions, according to cloud services firm Cloudflare (NET.N) and Amazon (AMZN.O) . "In the 10 hours before it was publicly announced, across the network we saw thousands of attempts to exploit it," Cloudflare CEO Matthew Prince said in a post on X late on Wednesday. "That jumped to tens of thousands in the 45 minutes post announcement, hundreds of thousands within 2 hours, and millions now." Amazon also said it saw widespread exploitation . IMPACT FROM JAPAN TO FINLAND Japanese companies including brokerage Nomura (8604.T) , lender Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group (8306.T) , airline ANA (9202.T) and East Japan Railway (9020.T) said on Thursday they were temporarily suspending some internet services as part of emergency measures. Brewer Asahi Group Holdings (2502.T) temporarily suspended certain websites and systems and was conducting a security impact assessment. Insurer Tokio Marine Holdings (8766.T) said it had suspended its group website. Japan's Ministry of Finance and Meteorological Agency partially suspended online services to implement safety measures, while Japan's National Tax Agency temporarily took down its service. The precautionary shutdowns show Japan's growing concerns over cybersecurity, as the country [USN:L1N45U0IU TEXT:"recorded"] more cyber incidents in the first nine months of the year than in all of last year, according to data from TrendAI. French telecoms group Orange (ORAN.PA) said it had temporarily suspended access to certain PHP-based websites and applications across several subsidiaries as a precaution. Tencent Cloud, one of China's largest cloud-computing providers, urged customers to install updated PHP versions but stopped short of calling for widespread website shutdowns. Finland's state IT services provider Valtori said it had continued installing PHP security patches overnight and was gradually lifting precautionary service blocks after [USN:S8N3WF054 TEXT:"shutting down"] government public web services a day earlier. "Restoring services can take days or even weeks, as in addition to updates, the systems need to be carefully tested," Valtori Director General Hannu Naumanen said in a statement. Valtori said the outages were not caused by exploitation of the vulnerabilities or by a cyber breach, and that it was not aware of any active exploitation of the flaws. SOME FIXES MAY TAKE WEEKS TO IMPLEMENT Several Asian governments ordered cybersecurity inspections related to the PHP vulnerabilities on Thursday. China's industry ministry urged organizations and users to inspect systems and upgrade to the latest secure version of PHP. It also recommended strengthening cybersecurity monitoring and changing accounts, passwords and keys where necessary. South Korea raised its private-sector cybersecurity alert level and activated emergency response measures, citing concerns over an increased risk of hacking attacks. Felix Kuhlenkamp, head of security at German digital industry association Bitkom, said that many larger operators had already carried out updates, but that for complex IT systems and smaller organizations it could take longer. "They may run a website using PHP but don't really keep a close eye on it," he said. "If a website is based on an old version of PHP for which there is no security update, the entire system must be updated."

item.title: Stocks drop as Meta fans AI worries, Treasuries gain
item.description: Stock indexes fell on Thursday, after Meta's earnings report reignited worries about the AI boom's heavy capital spending, sending investors to the safety of US Treasuries.
item.dc:creator: Caroline Valetkevitch, Amanda Cooper
item.content:encoded: Stock indexes fell on Thursday, after Meta's earnings report reignited worries about the AI boom's heavy capital spending, sending investors to the safety of US Treasuries. Brent crude hit a five-month high following Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia, which stoked concerns of further disruption to global energy supplies. The Nasdaq, weighed down by chip stocks, fell 2.6% in its biggest daily percentage drop since early June, while MSCI's All-World index (.MIWD00000PUS) was off 1.3%. Tech shares in Seoul, Tokyo, Amsterdam and Paris fell earlier. Shares of Meta Platforms (META.O) dropped 7% after reported quarterly results on Wednesday. Meta's third-quarter revenue beat expectations, but the company said it would [USN:L4N4671S3 TEXT:"issue"] non-voting stock, a plan that revived concern over its mounting capital commitments and the heavy spend of AI hyperscalers more generally. An index of semiconductors (.SOX) , among the biggest beneficiaries of AI spending, fell 6.7% in its biggest daily percentage decline since June 23. Shares of Tesla (TSLA.O) , which also reported earnings and cut its [USN:L4N4671SD TEXT:"spending forecast"], dropped 3.1%. Reuters reported that some Tesla insiders are concerned that CEO Elon Musk's public comments on a potential merger with SpaceX (SPCX.O) could invite shareholder scrutiny and complicate deal talks. Shares of SpaceX ended down 9%. Investors' shifting views over AI spending have added volatility to the market. The Nasdaq's Thursday selloff followed a 1% rally on Wednesday. "To the extent investors believe that those (AI) earnings are real... they are buyers of these stocks," said Rick Meckler, partner at Cherry Lane Investments, a family investment office in New Vernon, New Jersey. "But periodically, when they look at current earnings and the amount they're going to have to spend, they become concerned that these stocks are all overpriced." TREASURIES GAIN IN SAFETY PLAY US Treasuries rose, [USN:L6N4681A9 TEXT:"pushing yields lower"], as the stock market's fall boosted the safe-haven appeal of government debt. The yield on the benchmark US 10-year Treasury note was down 19.3 basis points at 4.953%, its biggest daily drop since March 10, 2023. It has dropped since rising to 5.3645% on October 7, highest since April 2002. Yields and prices move in opposite directions. "They are rotating out of techs, out of the AIs, and into the more safety trades, whether it's bonds or some of those big Dow Jones stocks," said Joe Saluzzi, partner and co-head of equity trading at Themis Trading. The Dow Jones Industrial Average (.DJI) rose 11.89 points to 52,867.98, the S&P 500 (.SPX) fell 93.74 points, or 1.2%, to 7,663.43 and the Nasdaq Composite (.IXIC) fell 694 points, or 2.6%, to 26,008.86. MSCI's gauge of stocks across the globe (.MIWD00000PUS) fell 14.95 points to 1,122.93, its biggest one-day fall since June. The pan-European STOXX 600 (.STOXX) index fell 1.05%. BRENT JUMPS ON ATTACKS Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia raised concerns of further disruption to energy supplies from the Middle East, pushing Brent oil up about 4%. Brent futures rose $4.35, or 4%, to settle at $113.17 a barrel, while US West Texas Intermediate crude rose $2.32, or 2.4%, to settle at $99.47. Fragile equity markets also boosted the yen, while the dollar rose against the euro. The Japanese yen strengthened 0.75% to 156.96 per dollar. The euro was down 0.09% at $1.1222. CONCERNS CONTINUE FOR FRANCE French markets were again hit on concerns over the country's strained public finances and ongoing street protests. France's 10-year government bond yields surpassed equivalent US Treasuries for the first time since 2013, reflecting growing over France's deteriorating fiscal position and rising debt burden. The benchmark 10-year yield was last up 6.5 basis points at 5.06%. [USN:L6N46814J TEXT:"The premium"] investors demand to hold French government debt over safe-haven German Bunds widened to its highest in 15 years.

ANKARA: Türkiye, Qatar, Pakistan, and Indonesia signed an agreement on Wednesday (Oct 21) to boost defence cooperation and strengthen defensive capabilities, the Turkish Defence Ministry said. In a statement, the ministry said the countries signed the Badr Memorandum of Understanding in Doha as a sign of their desire to further deepen cooperation and develop partnerships. "The agreement holds substantial economic importance," it said, adding the accord sought to foster cooperation in military production, boost military capabilities, and help collaboration in technical military training, research and development. "By leveraging the unique military production capabilities of each country, the initiative will facilitate cooperation and integration, enhance defence industrial capacities, and enable the fulfilment of the needs of allied and friendly nations," it added.

Show Less

Türkiye, which has NATO's second-largest army and a robust defence industry, has been helping Gulf nations, including Qatar, where it has a military base, bolster their defences amid the Iran war. In August, it signed a mutual defence pact with nuclear-armed Pakistan and Saudi Arabia, under which an attack on one party constitutes an attack on all. Ankara also has close ties with Indonesia, notably in the defence industry. The ministry said the Badr accord would strengthen ties between the countries' defence industries and bolster collaboration to promote security and achieve shared objectives. Haluk Gorgun, the chairman of Türkiye's Defence Industry Presidency, said the accord formed the foundation of a "strategic cooperation" to develop joint production and technology. "Technology sharing, joint development and strengthening domestic production capabilities lie at the heart of sustainable defence industry. As Türkiye, we value partnerships that go beyond off-the-shelf procurement models, that foster the development of a nation’s own human capital and industrial infrastructure," Gorgun said in a statement. "We believe that the Badr Memorandum of Understanding will contribute to transforming the complementary capabilities of Qatar, Pakistan, Indonesia, and Türkiye into concrete projects," he added.

item.title: Russia bombs Kyiv and Ukraine fires drones towards Moscow, despite talk of renewing negotiations
item.description: Russia pounded Kyiv with ballistic missiles and Ukraine sent hundreds of drones towards Moscow on Thursday, as the warring sides kept up a barrage of attacks despite the latest US push to end the conflict.
item.dc:creator: Olena Harmash
item.content:encoded: Russia pounded Kyiv with ballistic missiles and Ukraine sent hundreds of drones towards Moscow on Thursday, as the warring sides kept up a barrage of attacks despite the latest US push to end the conflict. US President Donald Trump [USN:L6N4681B6 TEXT:"said"] SpaceX (SPCX.O) CEO Elon Musk had restored Ukraine's Starlink access, one of the issues linked to a rift between Washington and Kyiv that has cast doubt on US support for Ukraine. Ukraine said Russia fired at least 21 ballistic missiles in three waves. President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said three carried cluster munitions — "bomblets" that disperse over a wide area and are banned by many countries because of the danger to civilians. Russia's defence ministry did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Russia said Ukraine launched 630 drones towards Moscow during the night. The two sides held an exchange of war dead, with Moscow handing over 252 bodies and Ukraine handing over 25, according to the Belta state news agency in neighbouring Belarus. Such exchanges have accompanied moves towards talks in the past. PUTIN: ENSURING SECURITY FOR RUSSIA, UKRAINE, EUROPE Russian President Vladimir Putin, interviewed on Russian television a day after meeting US presidential envoy Steve Witkoff, confirmed that [USN:L1N468183 TEXT:"Russia was ready"] to resume US-mediated talks with Ukraine next month. Putin said the aim of the talks was to ensure the security of Ukraine and Russia after the conflict was resolved. Witkoff, he said, had stressed that discussions had to extend to "the architecture of European security". "And I agree with that too. Well, let's see how things develop in the coming days." Zelenskiy [USN:L1N4670ZQ TEXT:"said he hoped"] negotiations, which would be the first since February, would take place early in November. Trump, in comments on Starlink, declined to say whether he had spoken to Musk about restoring the service for Ukraine. Earlier, the Wall Street Journal reported that Trump had called Musk and asked him to lift restrictions on Ukraine's use. "I don't want to comment on it, whether I called or whether somebody else called ... The bottom line - he put it back," Trump told reporters. Ukraine uses Starlink for battlefield communications and drone operations. Restricting the service hampered the country's attack and air defence drone missions against Russia. [USN:L8N4682IN TEXT:"Speaking"] earlier alongside Finland's prime minister, Zelenskiy said speed on Starlink systems had not been restored for Ukraine. "We are tackling that," Zelenskiy said, adding he hoped to discuss the issue with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio. A person familiar with the Starlink issue said the problem was continuing, with the same curbs largely remaining in place. Some drone units report reaching speeds of 200 kph (125 mph) with drones but otherwise the picture was unchanged, he said. “The main problem is that we have no official explanation what's going on," he said. RIFT BETWEEN WASHINGTON AND KYIV In more than a week of differences between Washington and Kyiv, Trump has repeatedly rebuked Ukraine for attacking Russian oil refineries while saying little about far deadlier Russian attacks on Ukraine. He called for Zelenskiy to be replaced and said Russia's actions in Ukraine have been "fine". Zelenskiy, who long avoided any criticism of the Trump administration, has increasingly pushed back against what he describes as a shift towards sympathy with Moscow. On Thursday, Zelenskiy snapped back at Witkoff for saluting Putin as a "humanitarian" during his visit to Russia, when the US envoy thanked Putin for [USN:L8N4670PP TEXT:"releasing a 74-year-old American"] captured by Russian forces in Ukraine. "Three waves of ballistic missiles have been launched at Kyiv by Russian 'humanitarians' since yesterday evening," Zelenskiy posted on X. "They used 21 missiles. Unfortunately, numerous sites across the city have been hit and damaged." Zelenskiy's meeting with Witkoff was aimed in part at repairing frayed relations with Washington after Trump announced a deal to buy Russian diesel and lifted sanctions on Moscow. Kyiv says Washington failed to provide early-warning data on Russian missile launches, throttled the SpaceX satellite system used to guide Ukrainian drones, and withheld missile defence systems bought on Ukreaine's behalf by Europeans. Washington denies shifting policies to hamper Ukrainian forces. After meeting Zelenskiy and European and NATO officials in Oslo this week, Witkoff spoke of "some degree of momentum", but the Kremlin expressed doubts. "The Americans sensed some new nuances (in Oslo) and told us about this. But these nuances, so to speak, do not entirely satisfy us," Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov said on Thursday. A senior Russian official, briefed on the Putin-Witkoff talks, said they were relatively short and not substantive. The American brought proposals drafted in Oslo and handed them to Putin for review, the person said. Another source close to the Kremlin said the US proposals included a scenario where Ukraine would cede its Donbas region to Russia in return for receiving a guarantee of its future security from NATO. Moscow has repeatedly said it would not end fighting unless Ukraine cedes more land, limits the size of its forces and is permanently barred from forming alliances. Ukraine dismisses Russia's conditions as a demand for capitulation that would leave it defenceless. ATTACKS IN MANY REGIONS Zelenskiy said two people were killed and 34 injured, including five children, in overnight attacks on a dozen Ukrainian regions. Regional officials said a Russian strike on a market in Lozova, near the northeastern city of Kharkiv, killed two people and injured 36. Three were killed in the southeastern city of Zaporizhzhia and one more in nearby Dnipropetrovsk region. Russia said it carried out a "massive strike" overnight on port infrastructure in Ukraine's Odesa region, as well as on vessels used by the Ukrainian military. In Russia, two people were wounded near Moscow by drones launched overnight towards the capital, Mayor Sergei Sobyanin [USN:P8N44K018 TEXT:"said"]. Most of the drones were downed at long range, he added.

item.title: Trump backs Ramaswamy attack ad as Republican Ohio governor condemns it
item.description: US President Donald Trump extolled an attack ad by Republican Vivek Ramaswamy against his Democratic rival in the close Ohio governor's race on Thursday, even as the state's Republican governor advised Ramaswamy to take it down.
item.dc:creator: Helen Coster
item.content:encoded: US President Donald Trump extolled an attack ad by Republican Vivek Ramaswamy against his Democratic rival in the close Ohio governor's race on Thursday, even as the state's Republican governor advised Ramaswamy to take it down. In the ad, Democratic candidate Amy Acton’s estranged mother, Donna Arthur, disputes Acton's account of a childhood involving homelessness and sexual abuse and urges Ohioans not to vote for her. In a Truth Social post, Trump advised Ramaswamy to keep running the ad. While not referring directly to the abuse allegations, Trump said: “let everyone listen to the mother of a defective, dishonest, and incapable Candidate, explain how the daughter is a DISASTER who, uncontrollably, lies, cheats, and steals!" Acton says she has not seen her mother since 1978. Acton's brother has supported her account of being sexually abused by her stepfather when she was a child. The stepfather, who died in 2004, was charged with rape. Opinion polls show Acton narrowly leading Ramaswamy, and analysts say the controversy could backfire on Republicans ahead of the November 3 midterms. 'IT'S JUST WRONG,' REPUBLICAN GOVERNOR SAYS Commenting on the ad, Ohio Governor Mike DeWine, a Republican, told reporters on Thursday: "It’s just wrong,” adding he would urge the Ramaswamy campaign to take down the ad. As the backlash built on Tuesday, Ramaswamy's campaign spokesperson Connie Luck issued a statement saying: "We don't know what happened between Amy and her mother ... but we know that Amy Acton is a serial fabulist." Acton's brother, Philip Stearns, called the ad a “desperate, disgusting attack,” while Acton campaign spokesperson Addie Bullock called Ramaswamy's decision to promote it “both despicable and entirely predictable.” Vice President JD Vance, campaigning on Wednesday with Ramaswamy and US Senator Jon Husted, an Ohio Republican, had brushed aside the blowback. Ramaswamy’s campaign said it was spending $4 million to promote the ad. David Cohen, a political science professor at the University of Akron, characterized the ad as "campaign malpractice.” Cohen said it could also mean trouble for Husted, who said in a statement that he would "not have run that ad" and who polls show trailing Democrat Sherrod Brown in a race that will help determine control of the US Senate. Among Republicans, Cohen predicted, "I think this will either encourage some people to switch parties, or more likely, you're going to have a lot of people staying home" on Election Day.

item.title: テンセントがオラクルからAI半導体10万個をリース、70億ドル規模－FT
item.description:
（ブルームバーグ）： 中国のテンセント・ホールディングス（騰訊）は、東南アジアでオラクルから先端のAI半導体を借り受けることで合意した。テンセントにとってAI半導体のリース契約としては過去最大規模となる。英紙フィナンシャル・タイムズ（FT）が事情に詳しい関係者の話として報じた。
報道によると、テンセントは、5年間の契約の一環として10万個の半導体を利用できるようになる。契約額は70億ドル（約1兆1000億円）に上るという。
中国のAI開発企業は米国の輸出規制を回避するため、米エヌビディア製など中国国内では入手できないAIアクセラレーターを海外で借りて利用している。中国のテクノロジー企業は、東南アジアのデータセンターの最大顧客層の一つとなっている。
テンセントとオラクルの担当者は、ブルームバーグ・ニュースのコメント要請に直ちに応じなかった。
原題：Tencent Leases AI Chips From Oracle
